Robson tested positive for methylamphetamine; he pleaded guilty to dangerous driving occasioning death and drug driving. He will be eligible for parole in October 2029.
items.title: Drug driver jailed for crash that killed a premature baby

items.summary: Alleged kitchen knife murderer Conor O'Neill, 40, has been denied bail after being charged with murder following the death of his partner. He is alleged to have stabbed her twice while driving in Palmerston, near Darwin. The case returns to court next month, where his lawyer says he will likely argue 'defensive conduct' at trial.
items.title: Conor O'Neill denied bail over partner's death

items.summary: As Türkiye prepares to host COP31 in Antalya, critics describe its climate targets and policies as critically insufficient. The country remains heavily reliant on coal, which accounted for 33 per cent of electricity generation last year, while solar and wind together reached nearly 23 per cent. Türkiye operates one of Europe's largest solar farms at Karapınar, but advocates say it lacks a roadmap to phase out fossil fuels, including gas. Total greenhouse gas emissions in 2024 reached 584.5 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent. Duygu Kutluay of Beyond Fossil Fuels warned the plans are not compatible with Türkiye's net-zero target by 2053.
items.title: COP31 Host Türkiye Faces Criticism Over Coal Reliance Ahead of Climate Summit

items.summary: On November 6th, 2026, Euronews aired its morning news bulletin, presenting a round-up of the most important stories from around Europe and beyond. The newsroom described it as delivering latest and breaking news across world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel within just a few minutes, framed with what it called independence and a European perspective.
items.title: Euronews Broadcasts Morning News Roundup Across Europe and Beyond

items.summary: Legal notices sent to Internet Freedom Foundation and Software Freedom Law Centre, purporting to come from the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and later backed by a Delhi Police “illegal content report,” turned out to be fabricated. An advisor Kanchan Gupta and RSS member Ratan Sharda denied on X that any such notices were sent; an anonymous police official told Scroll both documents are fake, noting the email address was likely created at 3.57 pm on October 29, 2026 – just six hours before it was used. The notice’s address traced to a different organisation registered in Nainital, and X later confirmed the notices came from an imposter while filing its own complaint.
items.title: Fake RSS and Delhi Police notices expose as hoax

items.summary: The Delhi Police arrested three contractors—Siraj, Tajuddin and Furkan—in connection with the collapse of a building under construction in Old Delhi’s Chawri Bazar that killed two persons. They were booked for culpable homicide not amounting to murder after police flagged unauthorised construction at the site five months earlier. The Municipal Corporation acknowledged an April warning about structural safety, alleging the owner used repairs as cover for new work. At least five remain feared trapped under debris.
items.title: Delhi Police Arrest Three Contractors Over Chawri Bazar Building Collapse

items.summary: During a hearing on Delhi's air quality, the Supreme Court identified the tradition of exchanging Diwali gifts as a contributor to vehicular pollution. The court made the remark while noting that the national capital continued to experience poor air conditions at the time.
items.title: Supreme Court Links Diwali Gift Culture to Delhi Air Pollution

items.summary: Parvinder Singh Jhota's family agreed to a post-mortem and ended its 22-day protest after talks with Punjab government representatives. The settlement followed the release of two arrested protesters on Thursday evening. The state accepted compensation of Rs 2 crore for the family, a job for his wife, a trauma centre in Jhota's memory, compensation for four injured people, and a memorial statue. Jhota was shot dead inside a medical store in Mansa on October 13 while hosting a Facebook Live session. His father Bhim Singh said last rites would be held Friday or Saturday after the family returns to Mansa with the body.
items.title: Jhota Family Agrees Post-Mortem, Ends Punjab Protest

items.summary: Palo Alto Networks is reportedly in talks to acquire Clutch Security, a startup securing AI agents' access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus milestone-based payouts. The Information first reported the discussions. Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million and now approaches $10 million ARR, implying about 50 times its revenue. Both companies declined comment.
items.title: Palo Alto Networks in Talks to Acquire AI Agent Security Startup Clutch

items.summary: For the first time, a refugee team competed at the Youth Olympics in Senegal. Created by the International Olympic Committee and managed by the Olympic Refuge Foundation, the athletes came from camps in Kenya and Uganda to compete in judo, taekwondo and track and field. Sprinter Florence Masumbe said she was proud to represent her country.
items.title: Refugee Team Competes at Senegal's First Youth Olympics

items.summary: Nashra Naim became the first woman vice-president of Aligarh Muslim University's students' union, which celebrates a 105-year history. Women candidates won six of 13 posts; Naim secured 7,091 votes against her nearest rival's 5,818. The elections followed an eight-year gap amid student protests and were declared by Prof Javaid Talib and Prof Nazia Hasan on Friday.
items.title: AMU Students' Union Elects First Woman Vice-President in Its History

items.summary: Banks across several Indian states will stay closed on multiple days in November 2026 as Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Puja, Bali Pratipada, Bhai Dooj and related regional festivals are observed. Closures fall on November 9, 10 and 11 depending on the state; for example, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttarakhand and Sikkim close on the 10th. Branch-dependent transactions such as large cash deposits or cheque processing may be delayed, but ATMs, UPI, internet banking and mobile apps remain available.
items.title: Indian Banks Close for Diwali and Regional Festivals in November

items.summary: The Election Commission, stung by a public row over alleged internal dissent following an Indian Express report, issued on November 4 orders assigning Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Pawan Kumar Sharma to supervise Director General of IT Seema Khanna and deploying Prakash Rajpurohit to share responsibilities with Maneesh Garg. The moves follow commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu's objections to a July 28 order, which they say was never implemented after being recalled on July 30.
items.title: Election Commission Adds Oversight for Two Officials in Dissent Dispute

items.summary: One officer was killed and three others wounded in a firefight with a suspect in Lakewood, a suburb of Denver, Colorado, on Thursday evening. The shooting followed police responding to a report of a suspicious person trying to board a public bus around 6.30pm. Police spokesperson John Romero said the man opened fire as officers arrived; it was unclear whether this happened inside or near the bus.
items.title: Officer Killed and Three Wounded in Colorado Firefight

items.summary: A Friday news roundup covers several developments, led by US President Donald Trump warning he may “destroy the rest” of Iran. The piece also reports Türkiye’s parliament approving a trilateral defense pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia (279 votes to 119), Israel's president Isaac Herzog saying government formation remains uncertain after consultations backing Gadi Eisenkot over Benjamin Netanyahu, Cristiano Ronaldo announcing his international retirement following November matches while continuing at Al Nassr, Harry Kane extending his Bayern Munich contract until June 30, 2029, Celtic beating Besiktas 3-2 in the Europa League, and US stock markets suffering their deepest one-day drop in 19 months as the Dow fell 1,834.84 points (3.44%) to 51,521.28.
items.title: Markets Plunge as Trump Threatens Iran and Ronaldo Announces Retirement

items.summary: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a retention option for ex-Agniveers, allowing those who fail to clear the merit cut after their initial four-year service under the Agnipath scheme to remain in Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) for two more years. The decision followed internal debates among CAPF chiefs and home ministry officials over how to assess merit without tests and where to post these highly trained soldiers, amid concerns about morale and integration with regular personnel who must pass three tests. Officials noted the quota increased from 10% to 50%, raising questions about direct induction versus competitive selection.
items.title: Cabinet Approves Agniveer Retention Option in CAPFs Amid Merit Debate

items.summary: President Donald Trump said he would review a 2022 law banning imports of Russian petroleum products but gave no timeline for change, reported ANI. He called the legislation possibly a bad law and agreed to look at it after being told by Congress signed it in 2022. The Treasury license covers only diesel until April 7, 2027, not all Russian oil.
items.title: Trump Reviews Law Banning Russian Petroleum Imports

items.summary: The Bhagya Lakshmi Temple at Charminar in Hyderabad opened round-the-clock from November 8 to 10 to distribute coins to devotees during Dhanteras celebrations. A large number of people turned up on Friday, with crowds swelling after the 7 am maharathi and continuing until midnight. Trustees Surya Prakash and Shashikala said coin distribution would begin at 7 pm on Sunday Diwali, with four entry and exit points provided for hassle-free darshan; police assisted in arrangements.
items.title: Bhagya Lakshmi Temple Opens Round-the-Clock for Dhanteras Coin Distribution

items.summary: A home tour of producer Anupriya Nagar's Juhu bungalow, featured on Curly Tales' YouTube channel, has drawn online attention amid speculation about her wealth. Though Hanuman Ansh reportedly grossed around Rs 420 crore worldwide, the article notes she was already affluent before its success.
items.title: Producer's Lavish Bungalow Sparks Wealth Speculation After Film Success

items.summary: Crude oil prices were heading for a sharp weekly decline as Brent crude and WTI shed 12% since Monday, driven by hopes that the Middle East war could end quickly after U.S. midterm results. At writing, Brent traded at $99.42 per barrel and WTI at $91.242, both up from Thursday’s close on reports of fresh tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts warn prices may stay supported but remain volatile amid uncertainty over escalation between the United States and Iran.
items.title: Oil Prices Face Weekly Drop Amid Tanker Attacks and Peace Hopes

items.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Thursday he is working to recast the stalled UK-Mauritius deal on the Chagos Islands so it better addresses US concerns over the Diego Garcia military base. The original 2025 treaty, signed under Keir Starmer, would have transferred sovereignty to Mauritius while leasing the base for 99 years; Britain was set to pay £165 million ($222 million) annually for three years, then £120 million thereafter. The pact remains unratified after President Donald Trump rejected it as “terrible” and “ridiculous,” putting implementation legislation on hold.
items.title: Burnham Seeks Revised Chagos Agreement Amid US Pressure

items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is urging businesses to publish salaries in job adverts now, rather than wait for compulsory legislation planned as soon as possible. The government argues the move helps first-time applicants and could prevent pay discrimination, following a consultation where 94% backed greater transparency. It follows an EHRC call for salary information access, amid falling disclosure rates on Adzuna (51%) and CIPD concerns over complex pay-setting.
items.title: Burnham urges firms to list pay in adverts ahead of new law

items.summary: Elon Musk has openly hoped to make SpaceX a competitor to Verizon and AT&T in mobile services, but Democrats’ strong showing in the 2026 midterms complicates that goal. Over the past month SpaceX bought an 800 MHz spectrum portfolio from Grain Management and struck a deal with Qualcomm for base stations. Lawmakers plan investigations into conflicts of interest, Musk’s federal contracts, his role regarding Ukraine’s internet access, and DOGE data handling.
items.title: Midterm Blue Wave Threatens SpaceX Mobile Plans

items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Small, the first model of its second Inkling generation and a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) with 594B total and 17B active parameters. It accepts text and image input and supports variable reasoning effort but does not support audio as of now. On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index it scores 31, up from 13 for its predecessor Inkling Small, ranking #4 of 29 in its price class. It scored 86. 3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 (Hard) and 13. 1% on Terminal-Bench 4. 0. Weights are closed at launch, with an Apache 2. 0 release planned after external safety testing and red-teaming. The model is live on Tinker for fine-tuning and inference. All scores come from the lab's benchmark table run at effort 0. 99 (xhigh) and temperature 1. 0; most rows use third-party evaluators such as Artificial Analysis, Scale AI and Vals. Prices are $0. 30 per 1M input tokens and $1.
items.title: Thinking Machines Lab Releases Multimodal MoE Model Inkling 2 Small

items.summary: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission directed the Bihar State Power Generation Company Limited to submit corrected tender documents for a proposed 150 MW solar project with a 300 MWh battery storage system in Bihar. The direction followed an October 12 hearing that found deficiencies, and BSPGCL had not yet filed updated versions of its Request for Selection document and draft power purchase agreement incorporating agreed modifications. BERC set November 9 as the deadline; the next hearing is scheduled for November 12 at 11:30 AM to consider the matter further.
items.title: BERC Orders BSPGCL To Fix Solar Tender Documents

items.summary: A fire broke out early Friday at a four-storey commercial building selling mobile accessories inside Puri Plaza, 13 Block, Chain Wali Gali, Gaffar Market, Karol Bagh. Around 20-25 fire engines were rushed to the spot, and no loss of life or injuries was reported; only property damage occurred. Delhi Police received a PCR call at around 1:28 am. Overheating or overcharging of batteries appears to be a possible cause, with the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) team examining the building for other combustible material while further action awaits investigation findings.
items.title: Delhi Fire in Karol Bagh Building Draws Emergency Response

items.summary: Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6, 2026, marking the start of Diwali. The page lists shubh muhurat times to buy gold, silver, vehicles, utensils and brooms in cities including New Delhi (6:02 PM–7:57 PM), Mumbai and Kolkata. Timings follow the New Delhi Panchang and may differ locally; even a small coin or utensil is said to invite blessings of Lakshmi, Dhanvantari and Kuber.
items.title: Dhanteras 2026 auspicious timings for buying gold, silver and utensils across India

items.summary: Sofia Liguori, a Google DeepMind research engineer and member of the Impact Accelerator team, resigned in October 2026 after becoming convinced her company was complicit in events in Gaza. Her concern centered on Project Nimbus, a $1.2bn deal signed with Israel in 2021 that built data centres there without allowing service denials to government entities. Liguori said she watched “a live-streamed genocide for a year,” knowing Google Cloud AI tools were available to Israeli state departments including the Ministry of Defense. After petitions and internal advocacy failed, she breached her non-disparagement agreement, posting her resignation letter publicly. This week, Alphabet told UK staff it would not enforce post-termination clauses against critics, which Liguori called a win for collective action. Google has not responded to openDemocracy’s request for comment at the time of publication.
items.title: Google Whistleblower Resigns Over Gaza Complicity

items.summary: IT services firm Coforge joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network on Friday, it said, to help companies integrate Grok's artificial intelligence portfolio. It will act as a Transformation Partner via its Momentuum Blue unit and Nuuron platform but did not disclose financial details.
items.title: Coforge Joins SpaceX Partner Network for Grok AI Tools

items.summary: Indian consumer inflation likely rose to 5.93% in October from 5.54% in September, per the median forecast of a November Reuters poll of 36 economists, nearing the RBI's upper target. Sharp food price rises—driven by a deficient monsoon and global pressures—lifted food inflation to about 8.20%, above its 7.74% prior level. Analysts at BofA Securities expect double-digit figures ahead; Union Bank of India's Kanika Pasricha says continued rate hikes may be prudent.
items.title: India Inflation Approaches Reserve Bank Upper Target Amid Food Price Surge

items.summary: Indian IT firm Coforge joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network on Nov 6, it said Friday, becoming a Transformation Partner to develop and deploy industry-specific Grok AI solutions. Deployments run through its Momentuum Blue unit using Nuuron platform services; financial terms were not disclosed.
items.title: Coforge joins SpaceX Grok partner network

items.summary: Google, Meta and TikTok filed separate federal lawsuits challenging a California law that takes effect on 1 January 2027 to protect children under-16 from addictive social media features. The companies argue the law violates their First Amendment rights and Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. California Attorney General Rob Bonta said it was reviewing the filings and remains committed to defending state laws protecting kids online.
items.title: Big Tech Sues California Over Child-Safety Social Media Law

items.summary: Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said in an X post on Friday. He did not specify whether output would move elsewhere or end entirely. The decision follows the truck's weak sales since its 2023 launch and repeated price revisions, as Tesla shifts focus to Cybercab for its robotaxi network.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Winddown by Mid-2027

items.summary: Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production at its Austin gigafactory around mid-next year, CEO Elon Musk said Friday, as the model struggles for mass-market appeal. The automaker did not immediately respond to a Reuters request. Musk framed the wind-down as enabling increased output of the newly launched Cybercab robotaxi model. Tesla does not disclose individual Cybertruck sales; it groups them in an Other Models category that delivered 8,295 units in Q3, down from 12,364 in Q2.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Wind-Down at Texas Factory

items.summary: Apple plans a software update that will review photos and files shared through the 'Anyone with the Link' option on iCloud Photos and Drive, raising privacy concerns. The change applies only to publicly linked content, not all stored files, and may block accounts if harmful material is found.
items.title: Apple to scan iCloud photos shared via public links in new update

items.summary: A report by the Berkeley nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research found Anthropic is improving its models around twice as fast as a year earlier, possibly because of recursive self-improvement. METR estimated this in analysis spanning about 11 weeks from mid-August through late October 2023 to 2025, though redactions limited detailed estimates and the group cautioned it may be overstating findings on well-specified tasks only. Anthropic co-founder Sam McCandlish said many conclusions matched his own view but noted redactions hinder independent checks. The report arrives as Anthropic prepares for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever.
items.title: Anthropic Accelerating AI Amid Safety Concerns

items.summary: New York City’s proposed Delivery Protection Act would require companies like Amazon to directly employ package drivers instead of delivery service providers, while adding safety and labor standards. The bill has Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s backing plus 31 of the council’s 51 members—enough to pass if voted on. Supporters say it improves street safety and protects workers; Amazon opposes it, warning it could put more than 5,000 small-business delivery employees at risk. Driver Luc Rene cites injuries from unsafe conditions as motivation for change.
items.title: NYC Council Bill Would Make Amazon Employ Its Delivery Drivers

items.summary:
Parents in North Carolina sued Google after their 13-year-old daughter, referred to as Emma in the complaint filed in California state court, spent months discussing suicidal thoughts with Gemini on her school-issued Chromebook. The lawsuit alleges that as Google integrates more AI into its products for schools, it exposes students to dangerous technology without warning parents or administrators. It claims Google marketed inherently dangerous Chromebooks as safe and exploited its trusted position in K-12 education. In response, Google said it is reviewing the claims and pointed to features like Guided Learning; a spokesperson noted extensive work with experts on safety resources. The complaint cites Gemini 3 Flash scoring just 7% of the time responding appropriately to mental-health messages. Amid criticism, Google moved this week to turn AI tools off by default for K-12 accounts, though schools re-enabling Search must accept its AI features.

visual:null},
items.title: North Carolina Parents Sue Google Over AI Mental Health Risk

items.summary: Elon Musk appears to have deleted posts urging Americans to vote Republican after Democrats won both chambers of Congress, per Forbes reporting on removed Election Day and October 29 messages. Grok confirmed the deletions when asked by an X user. Forbes noted Musk was the largest individual donor this cycle, giving at least $458 million to Republican-aligned causes, with about $216 million going to America PAC.
items.title: Musk Deletes Pro-Republican Posts After Democrats Win Midterms

items.summary: In Singapore, several digital brokerages are adding physical outlets as clients seek face-to-face trust in finance. uSMART opened two branches by October 2025 and plans four locations by end of 2026 to reach different market segments. Peer Moomoo already runs four storefronts, including a large Bugis hub with an in-house cafe, while Longbridge launched a networking cafe. Meanwhile, PhillipCapital blends its heritage online platform with eight community investor centres and self-employed adviser branches that draw steady walk-ins. Webull Singapore stays digital-first to avoid branch overhead costs, as executives note the industry is converging between traditional and online models.
items.title: Singapore Brokerages Blend Digital and Physical Branches

items.summary: Nashik police have reportedly named AIMIM leader and former MP Imtiaz Jaleel as a suspect in the TCS women's harassment and alleged religious conversion case. A case has allegedly been registered against him for providing shelter to Nida Khan, another accused person. The Special Investigation Team is probing the matter after reportedly recording his statement and collecting voice samples.
items.title: Former MP Imtiaz Jaleel Named Suspect in TCS Harassment and Conversion Case

items.summary: The New York Times reported that US authorities are investigating Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which purchases AI chips from Nvidia. House Foreign Affairs Committee chair Brian Mast and colleagues asked her to brief them on November 18 about the report's national security concerns. Nvidia declined to comment directly but said cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information rather than trade secrets tied to US national security, and that it always acts on government updates regarding parties of concern.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Called for Briefing Over Chinese Chip Allegations

items.summary: Ukraine’s Kyivstar raised its 2026 revenue guidance to a rise of 15%–17% in US dollar terms, up from 14%–16%, citing strong mobile demand and fast-growing digital services. Third-quarter EBITDA rose 10.3% to US$189 million as digital revenue jumped 68.9%. CEO Oleksandr Komarov said the company did not factor an end to the war into its forecast, which it has yet to publish for 2027.
items.title: Kyivstar Raises Revenue Guidance on Digital Growth

items.summary: A new mapping by Embrapa found that cacao-growing area in Pará rose about a third between 2022 and 2024 to 116,436 hectares (287,700 acres), with roughly 96% on land cleared before 2020. The pattern positions Amazon cacao as compliant with the EU’s Deforestation Regulation, which bars cocoa from land deforested after Dec. 31, 2020. Most new plantings are full-sun monocultures rather than shaded agroforestry, a less sustainable shift driven by record prices that pushed West African farmers to clear forest. CocoaAction Brasil and researchers say Brazil can grow more on existing cleared land without clearing native vegetation. Venturieri warns there is still risk but notes open pasture makes new clearing uneconomic. The EU imports about 60% of global cocoa, making traceability a priority for the sector's export ambitions.
items.title: Brazilian cacao spreads on old land, not forest

items.summary: FOB China prices for n-type M10 and 210R wafers held steady week on week at $0.146/pc and $0.153/pc, per the OPIS Global Solar Markets Report released Nov. 3. Stability is attributed to firm polysilicon prices and improving supply-demand dynamics in solar cells driven by overseas demand and domestic installation activity. However, oversupply and elevated inventories—estimated at up to 30 GW—keep fundamentals weak, with leading producers running around 45%-50% capacity. The price outlook stays subdued unless downstream demand holds; once polysilicon prices fall, wafer prices are expected to follow.
items.title: China Wafer Prices Hold Steady on Firm Polysilicon Despite Weak Fundamentals

items.summary: Four coaches of the Karmabhoomi Express caught fire near Sarai Banjara in Punjab, prompting concern over the incident. The cause and extent of the damage remain to be determined, with no immediate information on what triggered the blaze or whether any passengers were injured. Officials say further details regarding the circumstances are awaited as this developing story continues.
items.title: Karmabhoomi Express Coaches Catch Fire in Punjab

items.summary: The Supreme Court issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) after a viral social media post from its official X account targeted Chief Justice Surya Kant. The court said freedom of expression cannot shield interference with justice and that any attempt to undermine judicial authority must be dealt with an iron hand, citing a complaint registered as a writ petition on October 30 following one lodged by advocate Vineet Jindal on October 13.
items.title: Supreme Court issues contempt notice to Kerala Congress over CJI-targeting post

items.summary: A report released Thursday at Shanghai's ninth China International Import Expo highlights China's growing role as a global import market. It shows China's share of global exports rose from 3.2% in 2000 to 9.2% in 2025, with Belt and Road partner country exports reaching 59.4%. The report was jointly compiled by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of World Economics and Politics and UNCTAD's Division on International Trade and Commodities.
items.title: China's Growing Role as Global Import Market Highlighted in Report

items.summary: In a Hot Take episode, CGTN's Yang Zhao spoke with experts in Xiamen about protecting marine life beyond national borders after the BBNJ Agreement entered into force in January 2026. The treaty offers countries a way to create marine protected areas in international waters. Experts discussed what is needed to implement it and why open-ocean health matters.
items.title: Experts Discuss Protecting the High Seas Under New Treaty

items.summary: Xiamen's World Ocean Week offered the public a rare chance to climb inside a full-scale simulator of China's Jiaolong manned submersible. The event featured CGTN's Liu Jiaxin, who took a simulated dive with a real pilot to experience 7,000-meter pressure firsthand. Jiaolong is China's first operational deep-sea manned submersible, designed for depths up to 7,000 meters.
items.title: Public Simulated Dive Inside China's Jiaolong Submersible

items.summary: The 2026 World Ocean Week opened Thursday in southeast China's Fujian Province, where global ocean experts gathered to strengthen international cooperation on marine protection. The event coincided with China unveiling new scientific tools and programs for conservation and governance. Participants emphasized that conserving connected ecosystems requires cross-border collaboration beyond individual nations.
items.title: China Opens World Ocean Week in Xiamen Amid BBNJ Bid Push

items.summary: Major tech firms saw their stock values fall after a sell-off by investors following the US midterm elections, with the decline blamed on an expectation of a slowdown in AI development. The article explains how this affects everyday finances: pension savers holding defined contribution pensions may see reduced savings value, and those near retirement could receive less income if they cash in too soon. It also notes possible effects on jobs and prices through currency movements. Experts advise against panic selling, urge diversification, and stress that investments require a long-term outlook.
items.title: UK investors weigh impact of global tech share fall

items.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order declaring the renovated Oval Office a national monument, saying it will not be altered or destroyed by future presidents. The order does not block changes to decor or furnishings. It follows his renovation of the room and comes after he demolished part of the East Wing without congressional approval. Legal experts say its effect is unclear, as revoking such designations has not been tested in court.
items.title: Trump Signs Order Preserving Oval Office as National Monument

items.summary: Three weeks after lung cancer surgery that had put his travels in doubt, Pope Leo XIV is beginning a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay. He will arrive in Montevideo and spend three days there before traveling to Argentina and returning home to Peru. Vatican communications chief Maria Montserrat Alvar said the pope's stamina was fantastic and that doctors are confident he has passed his 14-day recovery period, noting tickets for his prayer vigil sold out within two days. Some experts doubt the visit will revive Catholicism in Uruguay.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Begins Latin America Tour After Cancer Surgery

items.summary: Carbon Brief's latest state of the climate update analyses forecasts from more than a dozen climate models and six global temperature datasets, projecting this year's super El Niño to peak at around 4C by end-2026. Zeke Hausfather called it 'simply staggering.' Carbon Brief estimates roughly a 96% chance that 2027 becomes the warmest year on record.
items.title: Carbon Brief projects 'super El Niño' peaks in December

items.summary: Airlines and airports across Europe are on high alert after a wave of hoax bomb threats targeted commercial flights this week, leaving at least 35 planes searched or diverted. One incident drew scrutiny: an Aer Lingus pilot flying from Dublin to Rome reportedly insisted on landing at a civilian airport instead of the Évreux military base, prompting two fighter jets to intercept the aircraft. French prosecutor Rémi Coutin said the pilot and co-pilot would be questioned, noting he could bring charges for refusing cooperation; Aer Lingus defended them as professional.
items.title: European Airlines Brace After Wave of Hoax Bomb Threats

items.summary: European stock markets fell sharply after a steep drop in US technology shares spread across the Atlantic, with analysts blaming Democrats' midterm gains for sparking worries about an AI industry slowdown. The FTSE 100 opened down 1.5%, or 166 points, to 10,615, led by AstraZeneca's 2.8% fall. Elsewhere, Germany's Dax dropped 1.5% and Japan's Nikkei sank 6%. Despite the losses, most indices remain up for the year.
items.title: European markets slide as AI slowdown fears follow US tech rout

items.summary: Andy Burnham announced employers will be legally required to publish salaries in job adverts, aiming to empower employees and jobseekers with fairer pay information. The move follows a July consultation that the government said 93% of businesses responded positively to. Experts warn omitting pay details disadvantages young people and women, while ministers have yet to decide what must be published or how it will be enforced.
items.title: Burnham announces legal pay disclosure on job ads

items.summary: A CGTN report titled “How to win big: betting on the US midterms” explains that prediction-market betting has grown in popularity, with more people placing picks and cash on major 2026 U.S. midterm-election races. The piece features an interview between CGTN’s Martin Markovitz and one bettor about his choices and how he makes them.
items.title: CGTN profiles a bettor on US midterm races

items.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his term, escalating a standoff between the presidency and judiciary. The court declared his dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed null and void, rejecting claims it followed complaints about justice administration. Opposition groups accuse him of prolonging rule through constitutional changes; he insists reforms enable democratic elections. Somalia last held nationwide direct elections in 1969 after more than 30 years of civil war.
items.title: Somalia's Supreme Court Rejects President's Term Extension Amid Political Crisis

items.summary: Protests over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) dam in Arunachal Pradesh have escalated into violence, arrests and a heavy security deployment. The state frames the project as a safeguard against China’s upstream hydropower scheme, while residents fear losing their land and river; it is projected to generate roughly 11,200 MW of power. After four protesters were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in early October, clashes on October 23 left police filing at least eight cases and arresting 26 people. Security companies rose from seven till October 22 to around 10 to 12 by November 3, with 250 Rapid Action Force personnel reportedly sent to Pasighat. Protest groups refuse peace talks until detainees are released; SAAYA’s Geni Nangkar said they would not meet the chief minister until demands were met. A legal adviser added release is within the government’s power and could be decided tonight if there was political will. The dam may affect 27 villages, with a livelihood scheme having disbursed about ₹8.05 crores to 322 households since September. Residents reject moving for compensation, saying they would live and die on their land. A central demand is the withdrawal of central forces; a 300-kilometre march continues to press release of detainees, talks before construction, revocation of suspension orders and force withdrawal. The advisory board under APUAPA heard detention cases on October 30 without deciding them, while a writ petition was set for November 10. Mongabay-India reported the figures; one allegation that residents were offered ₹2.5 lakhs to sign MoUs could not be independently verified.
items.title: Protesters Reject Talks Over Siang Dam Amid Security Build-up

items.summary: The UN climate summit COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye on November 9 amid wars and energy insecurity that are pulling governments toward short-term national interests. Its agenda covers adaptation, emissions reduction, finance and a just transition, alongside the Turkish host’s electrification pledge to raise electricity’s share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035 and Brazil’s voluntary fossil fuel exit roadmap through 2033. Evidence is stark: the World Meteorological Organization confirms 2015-25 were the 11 hottest years on record, and UN data estimates developing countries will need about $305 billion a year by 2035 for adaptation against roughly $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion received in 2024. Officials warn preparedness lags as overshoot of the Paris goal becomes likely.
items.title: UN Climate Summit Opens Amid Energy Insecurity and Modest Progress Expectations

items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government announced Friday a package of emergency cybersecurity measures to address Japan's escalating cyber threats. The plan includes forming a team of top-gun specialists focused on penetration testing and strengthening defenses, plus deploying an expert group combining government officials and private-sector partners to support companies under attack. Officials attribute the surge in high-profile incidents this year partly to AI capabilities and weak security practices.
items.title: Takaichi Government Unveils Emergency Cybersecurity Measures Amid Rising AI-Linked Attacks

items.summary: A juvenile orangutan seized in Mumbai in 2024 has been repatriated to Sumatra after two years of delays. Yogesh Nilkand Warkad called it the first successful CITES animal return from India. The move draws focus on five infant orangutans rescued in Odisha, estimated at 1 and 1.5 years old, held at Nandankanan Zoological Park while their origins are investigated. Indonesia plans a seven-member delegation to assess them; experts say release could come in about four years.
items.title: India Repatriates Seized Orangutan, Hopes Rise for Five More

items.summary: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak paid a $12 million fine on Friday, his party UMNO has said. The payment lets him serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest. UMNO stated it completed all court payments this morning. Razak was jailed at 73 over his role in one of the largest-ever global plunders of sovereign wealth fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad.
items.title: Jailed Malaysian ex-PM Najib pays fine, meeting condition for house arrest

items.summary: Canary Media reports that the latest Clean Investment Monitor shows the U.S. solar supply chain is largely onshored: domestic module production exceeds annual installations of 47.9 gigawatts, and cell output reached up to 19.5 GW after factory openings this year. However, polysilicon and wafer production lag behind. The Rhodium Group modeled post-2030 scenarios projecting an average of between 8 and 52 GW annually, noting that installations may fall once federal tax credits expire.
items.title: Canary Media Examines U.S. Solar Supply Chain Progress and Gaps

items.summary: As Indians celebrate Dhanteras, many visit jewellery stores for gold and silver, while others buy a broom (jhaadu) from local vendors. The tradition is rooted in the belief that bringing a new broom home invites Goddess Lakshmi's blessings and drives away negative energy. Since Lakshmi favors clean homes, sweeping with a broom symbolizes removing dust and misfortune to welcome prosperity. Dhanteras 2026 falls on Friday, November 6, after Trayodashi begins around 10:30 am. A broom may cost around ₹50 or ₹100, making it an affordable way for anyone from a daily-wage worker to participate in the festival's customs of prayer and cleanliness before evening puja.
items.title: Why Indians Buy a Broom on Dhanteras Instead of Gold or Silver

items.summary: Poland has warned European allies not to negotiate an end to Russia's war in Ukraine without accounting for the security interests of Eastern Europe, which it says is most exposed to spillover effects. Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said Western Europe must not deal with Russia 'over the heads of the east Europeans,' while Prime Minister Donald Tusk urged counterparts to be careful about President Putin's intentions and realistic about US-led talks. Warsaw opposes a plan, reportedly floated by US negotiators, to restart Russian gas imports, which Polish Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka called 'absurd.' The warnings come ahead of trilateral Ukraine-Russia-US talks in Abu Dhabi next week.
items.title: Poland Warns Allies Not to Settle Ukraine War Over Eastern Europe

items.summary: Türkiye aims for 175 GW of solar and wind capacity by 2040, per its new national energy policy. Minister Alparslan Bayraktar presented the vision ahead of COP31 in Antalya, noting total installed power will rise to 281 GW with renewables reaching 77% from 63%. Reaching the goal would cost around $190 billion, roughly $100 billion for new solar and wind projects. The plan emphasizes distributed systems up to 1 MW and expanded storage capacity of 140 GWh.
items.title: Türkiye Sets Renewable Energy Targets for 2040

items.summary: A Baltimore city circuit court judge this summer ruled that PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, and other companies should not be held liable under public nuisance claims for plastic pollution, since the sale of single-use plastics is lawful. Judge Audrey J.S. Carrión wrote that companies conducting lawful activities “should not be held liable… because others are misusing the products in an unlawful manner.” The decision reflects a broader pattern: similar reasoning has scuttled New York’s public nuisance suit against PepsiCo and Frito-Lay, with comparable cases from Missouri to California. Environmental advocates argue manufacturers knew pollution was foreseeable — the word “foreseeable” appears 22 times in Baltimore’s complaint — but courts remain skeptical of extending liability past lawful sale.
items.title: Baltimore Court Rejects Corporate Liability for Plastic Pollution

items.summary: Labor MP Jayne Stinson says staff found balloons outside and in the car park of her Plympton electorate office. She said the matter turned dark when it became clear they carried threats to her safety, sexist names and other abuse; one balloon reportedly contained powder that covered a staffer who popped it. SA Police are investigating amid an increase in threats toward elected representatives.
items.title: South Australian MP reports threatening, sexist messages on balloons left at her office

items.summary: A webpage invites readers seeking opportunities in the world's second-largest economy to note that China is opening more doors. It states imports are set to exceed $3 trillion in 2026, alongside expanding trade ties and growing market access creating fresh business opportunities globally.
items.title: China Opens Trade Doors as Imports Set for Record in 2026

items.summary: A bomb threat email sent to the Bombay High Court also named the Bombay Stock Exchange, Mahalaxmi Racecourse and actor Amitabh Bachchan's Juhu residence, prompting a security alert in Mumbai. Police and security agencies are investigating to identify the sender. The message warned of a grenade attack at a school on October 31 and threatened his residence between October 31 and November 27. It also targeted Diljit Dosanjh's concert on November 27. Bachchan, then 84, greeted fans from behind a bulletproof enclosure.
items.title: Bomb Threat Email Targets Mumbai Court, Racecourse and Bachchan Residence

items.summary: A court denied bail to Craig Langford, a 51-year-old man from Werribee accused of sending violent death threats and sexualised slurs to Melbourne Cup-winning jockey Michelle Payne over three days last week via Instagram. Prosecutors cited grave concerns for her physical safety and mental health after the alleged threats left her in shock. The magistrate deemed him an unacceptable risk, though Langford denied sending the messages during questioning. He will return next month.
items.title: Stalker Denied Bail Over Death Threats To Michelle Payne

items.summary: According to the Qatari Emiri Diwan, Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on Friday to discuss de-escalating regional tensions. The leaders addressed strategic relations between their countries and Doha's mediation efforts toward 'a comprehensive agreement that resolves the crisis.' Qatar, alongside Pakistan, has mediated since war began with late February attacks on Iran.
items.title: Qatari Emir and Trump Discuss De-escalation of US-Iran Tensions

items.summary: The excerpt from Abhijeet Kolapkar’s book How to Be Debt Free argues that personal loans are more beneficial than withdrawing from provident funds over the long term. It opens with eight rules for borrowing responsibly, including keeping EMIs under 40% of monthly income and avoiding use for investments or luxury spending. Two examples illustrate lost compounding: Sudhir withdrew Rs 4,00,000 at age 35; leaving it until 60 would have grown to about Rs 27,39,390 at 8%, a loss of nearly Rs 23.39 lakh. Amit’s PPF balance reached Rs 43,98,642 after 15 years but would fall to ₹28,11,768 with an early withdrawal. In Sudhir’s case, a five-year loan at 12% would cost about Rs 1,34,000 in interest yet preserve the PF growth of Rs 27.39 lakh. The piece advises treating loans as temporary and maintaining an emergency fund equal to 6–12 months of expenses before considering withdrawal from long-term savings.
items.title: Personal Loans Beat PF Withdrawals for Financial Stability

items.summary: Paul Mackenzie, leader of a Kenyan starvation cult, faces possible execution after being convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult between January 2021 and September 2023. Hundreds of bodies have been found since 2023 at the sect's base near Malindi in what became known as the Shakahola Forest Massacre. The Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions urged the court to impose capital punishment, while Mackenzie plans to appeal.
items.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Sentenced for Child Murders Faces Death Penalty

items.summary: A fire engulfed four coaches of the Karmabhoomi Express near Sarai Banjara, close to Rajpura, on Friday. Officials say it reportedly started in the train's pantry before spreading to adjoining coaches and was brought under control after a fire alarm let passengers evacuate. Himanshu Aggarwal, Patiala Deputy Commissioner, said teams rushed to the spot and no casualties have been reported so far. The Railways has ordered a high-level inquiry into the cause.
items.title: Fire Engulfs Four Coaches of Karmabhoomi Express in Punjab

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah addressed BJP workers at the Parade Ground in Dehradun, attacking Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for allegedly protecting infiltrators and spreading a false narrative. Shah reiterated his party's agenda to detect, delete and deport infiltrators while highlighting Uttarakhand's Uniform Civil Code implementation. Recalling past election tallies, he set a target of winning over 65 seats in the state assembly. Separately, a news bulletin covered southern India developments including Karnataka ethanol blending reaching up to 31.2 percent and a bomb threat email targeting Mumbai landmarks.
items.title: Shah Attacks Gandhi Over Infiltrators, Sets Election Target in Dehradun

items.summary: A bus crashed Friday morning in eastern France near the Swiss border, local authorities said, leaving several victims. Education minister Edouard Geffray identified it as a school bus, while the area prefect said an intercity bus was involved, Reuters reported. Transport minister Philippe Tabarot said he was heading to the scene. The exact number of victims and crash circumstances remain awaited.
items.title: Bus Crash Near Swiss Border Leaves Several Victims in France

items.summary: The India Fix newsletter by Shoaib Daniyal compares two cases of punishing people for offending religious sentiments. Last month, a Saudi court sentenced Sri Lankan Anojan Sivarasa to death over an allegedly derogatory comment about Islam and Prophet Muhammad; global anger forced the state to overturn his sentence, though he remains jailed. Closer home, on October 28, an Indian court gave three Muslim men life sentences with hard labour for killing cows. The judge cited Hindu texts like the Vedas and Manusmriti, saying “33 crore Hindu gods are believed to reside in them.” Daniyal argues India’s anti-beef laws enshrine a similar idea that insulting faith can be punished by law, while acknowledging vast differences: India has a secular constitution, unlike Saudi Arabia. He links modern vigilante violence against Muslims accused of cow-related crimes to forces seeking to roll back 1949 decisions.”},
items.title: India's anti-beef laws mirror Saudi blasphemy punishments

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that linking social welfare benefits to voter ID instead of Aadhaar could exclude people whose names are deleted from electoral rolls during the SIR exercise. He called it 'rights theft' and a conspiracy benefiting the BJP, saying anyone who voted against them would have their name struck off. The Congress had earlier attacked Union minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh's remarks that an EPIC number with biometric authentication will be required for Panchayati Raj benefits. PTI reported the exchange on Nov 6.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi calls voter ID welfare rule rights theft, blames Modi government

items.summary: The Madurai City Central Crime Branch arrested former deputy Mayor and AIADMK functionary P M Mannan on Friday, Nov 6, for allegedly attempting to bribe a ruling TVK MLA during a possible no-confidence motion against the C. K. Jayalalithaa-led government. Police reportedly interrogated him for over four hours.
items.title: Former Madurai Deputy Mayor Arrested Over Bid to Topple TVK Government

items.summary: Sai Life Sciences Ltd reported a net profit of Rs 98 crore for the September 2026 quarter, up from Rs 84 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose to Rs 659 crore from Rs 537 crore, a 23% increase. EBITDA grew 20% to Rs 187 crore, while PAT margin eased to 15% from 16%. CEO Krishna Kanumuri cited strong business momentum and expanding global partnerships.
items.title: Sai Life Sciences Shares Jump After Strong Q2 Results

items.summary: Indian equities defied global trends on Friday as the Sensex rose over 1,000 points and Nifty50 climbed past 24,700. The rally followed a sharp worldwide sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks after US Democrats defeated Republicans in midterm elections raising regulatory fears. Foreign investors posted net buying of Rs 14,975 crore on Thursday, their largest single-day gain in years, while analysts cited strong earnings as fundamental support.
items.title: Sensex Surges Over 1,000 Points Amid Global AI Sell-off

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to suspend the 10-year sentence imposed by the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court on journalist Tarun Tejpal over a 2013 rape case. A two-justice bench declined his bail plea, stating it found no fit ground for suspension and was concerned only with that question alone.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Suspension of Tarun Tejpal's Sentence in 2013 Case

items.summary: Security agencies launched an investigation on Friday after a bomb threat email targeted Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow Jalsa, the Bombay High Court and Mumbai's Mahalaxmi Racecourse. Police said the email threatened to blow up these sites, including the racecourse scheduled to host Diljit Dosanjh's concert later this month. Authorities later confirmed the threat was a hoax.
items.title: Bombay HC Confirms Bomb Threat Email Against Bachchan Bungalow Was Hoax

items.summary: Thousands protested in Paraguay over a banking scandal involving the freezing of savers' funds at Ueno Bank, affecting three million customers. Demonstrators held placards and burned an effigy of President Santiago Peña, demanding impeachment rather than resignation. Congress has placed his resignation on hold while proceedings continue.
items.title: Paraguay Protesters Demand President's Impeachment Over Banking Crisis

items.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 4,588 crore in Q2FY27, up 25% from Rs 3,673.32 crore a year earlier, with revenue rising to Rs 57,514.98 crore. The company attributed the growth mainly to strong automotive demand, noting SUV volumes rose 26% and EVs held their market lead. Group CEO Anish Shah said results reflect resilient execution across businesses despite macro headwinds. Shares gained about 3%, having risen roughly 12% over the past month. Separately, M&M announced Shuchi Suri would move to Chief Sales and Marketing Officer of its automotive business from April 1, 2027.
items.title: Mahindra Profit Jumps as Auto Sales Drive Q2 Gains

items.summary: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Austin gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Nov 6. Sales have been weak: Kelley Blue Book reported just 20,237 Cybertrucks sold in the United States in 2025, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, against a pre-launch prediction of 250,000 units. The wind-down would free capacity for the newly launched Cybercab model central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions.
items.title: Tesla winds down Cybertruck production for robotaxi pivot

items.summary:
Global investors are pressing South Korean conglomerates to speed up corporate governance reforms, but progress has been uneven. Samsung Electronics illustrates the resistance: it reported record quarterly operating profit yet trades at 1.87 times book value versus Nvidia's 29 and Apple's 44. Activist Life Asset Management asked Samsung to review its decision to defer deploying remaining shareholder-return funds until January, while Palliser Capital called for buybacks at Samsung and Hyundai Motor. Banks have largely complied with reforms, but large chaebol affiliates are resisting as their lobbying intensifies, raising concerns the momentum behind President Lee Jae Myung's drive could stall.

visual null
items.title: Samsung Resists Corporate Reforms as Investors Push Back on South Korea's Biggest Chaebol

items.summary: The European Commission charged TikTok on Friday with failing to protect users’ mental health, saying its algorithm can be harmful and leads vulnerable young people down rabbit holes they cannot easily escape. The preliminary finding under the Digital Services Act says safeguards against repetitive content are ineffective. TikTok called the findings false and meritless and said it would challenge them; officials could fine it up to 6% of global turnover.
items.title: EU Charges TikTok Over Harmful Mental Health Content

items.summary: On November 6, Amazon announced that US customers could use its AI-powered assistant, Alexa for Shopping, to search and buy products through text messages. The feature lets users research items, compare prices, track deals, and complete purchases on their behalf. It is rolling out first to a small group of invited customers before a broader launch in the coming weeks.
items.title: Amazon Expands Alexa for Shopping via Text Messages

items.summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory by mid-2026 to free the plant for the Cybercab self-driving taxi. The move ends a struggling launch, with deliveries of only 8,300 trucks in one quarter against an aim of 200,000 yearly. Musk has instead bet on robotics and artificial intelligence.
items.title: Musk shifts Tesla focus away from Cybertruck toward robots and AI

items.summary: Protesters broke into a construction site for a Microsoft AI data centre in Amsterdam on Friday, opening two days of rallies across 16 countries. The Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition backs the actions calling to pause large-scale construction over resource and climate concerns. Pure Data Centres plans more than $1 billion investment and urged protesters to leave safely. EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said Europe needs data centres but with care, warning of rising energy bills and environmental damage.
items.title: Activists Breach Microsoft Data Centre Site Amid Europe-Wide Protests

items.summary: Brussels warned TikTok on Friday that it must change the design of its personalised For You feed or risk large fines under the Digital Services Act, after finding preliminary evidence of violations. The European Commission said the algorithm's 'rabbit hole' effect repeatedly recommends similar content, potentially exposing children to harmful material about sadness and body image. TikTok rejected the findings as fundamentally inaccurate, saying they misrepresent how its platform works while maintaining a strong record of protecting users.
items.title: EU Orders TikTok To Overhaul For You Feed Amid Child Safety Concerns

items.summary: Elon Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production next year, though he did not say whether it fully stops or moves elsewhere. Lead engineer Wes Morrill suggested the vehicle is being discontinued, living on through the self-driving Cybercab. Fans mourn online; critics and recalls weighed in earlier.
items.title: Musk Signals Cybertruck Production Wind-Down at Texas Factory

items.summary: Tesla raised US Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and stopped accepting orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim, making the cheapest orderable model $92,490. The move follows Tesla's confirmation it will end production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027. This is the second price increase in under three months; Premium AWD prices rose 15.6% since early August and entry prices jumped 32%. Analysts say higher prices on a truck with falling demand signal a wind-down, pushing buyers toward higher-margin trims before production ends around mid-2027.
items.title: Tesla Raises Cybertruck Prices Before Ending Production

items.summary: Goldman Sachs limited access to Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft GitHub to engineers, per October internal guidance seen by Bloomberg. Traders and bankers who used these tools for months lost them after a productivity and risk review. Spokesperson Nick Carcaterra said the firm offers AI tools during trials before handing them to best-suited staff. The move reverses July praise from CIO Marco Argenti for traders' 'vibe coding.' Goldman still built an in-house assistant combining OpenAI, Anthropic, and Alphabet models.
items.title: Goldman Sachs Restricts AI Coding Tools to Engineers and Strats

items.summary: The European Commission said in preliminary findings that TikTok's recommendation algorithm may repeatedly expose users, especially minors and vulnerable adults, to harmful content such as videos on mental health struggles, weight loss and body image. The bloc found TikTok failed to adequately assess or mitigate these risks. If confirmed, the commission could impose a fine of up to 6% of TikTok's global annual turnover under Digital Services Act proceedings.
items.title: EU Flags TikTok's Feed as Risk of Harmful Content

items.summary: AI company Anthropic introduced a new Personal Finance feature in its chatbot Claude, helping users track bank and credit card spending. The beta is available only in the United States for Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Personal Finance Feature to Claude AI Chatbot

items.summary: Parents of a 13-year-old girl sued Google in California, alleging she used the company's AI-powered search on a school-issued Chromebook to plan her suicide. Filed Monday 2 November, it is believed to be the first such negligence claim over school-blocked AI features. The complaint says Emma had no mental illness history before entering a psychological crisis after using the engine. Google says its AI Mode includes self-harm safeguards and is reviewing the claims; attorney Andrew Liddell urged schools to keep search off until safety measures improve.
items.title: Parents Sue Google Over AI Search and a Teen's Suicide

items.summary: Tribal leader Nisha Kumari Bhagat was found dead at her Ranchi residence on Friday, hours after allegedly going live on Facebook. Police suspect suicide but say circumstances remain unestablished. In the nearly 11-minute video, she cried and alleged that speaking out against the Hemant Soren government meant inviting death. Opposition leader Babulal Marandi expressed grief, alleging harassment for defending tribal rights, and called for chief minister Hemant Soren to resign.
items.title: Jharkhand tribal leader dies by suicide after Facebook Live post

items.summary: Tesla is ending Cybertruck production, with CEO Elon Musk announcing Friday that the automaker will wind down the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027. Tesla says it wants to free capacity for more Cybercab output, though analysts note Giga Texas has ample idle space and Cybercab volumes are low. The truck sells at roughly a tenth of its planned 250,000-unit annual line, with estimated deliveries near 30,000 units a year versus installed capacity above 125,000. Tesla does not break out Cybertruck sales separately, lumping them into Other Models, which fell 48% in Q3 2026 to 8,295 units. The item notes no details yet on inventory or owner service plans.
items.title: Tesla Ends Cybertruck Production Citing Weak Sales

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Anthropic faces investor resistance over its proposed $1.5 trillion initial public offering, following a sharp decline in US technology stocks. Three prospective investors want the valuation lowered; one suggested about $1 trillion and another cut the target to around $80 billion. Company executives are expected to review plans shortly, with no final decisions announced.
items.title: Anthropic IPO Valuation Meets Investor Resistance Amid Tech Selloff

items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a model designed to find and exploit security flaws, to vetted Daybreak Red customers on Thursday, rating it 'Critical' under its safety framework. OpenAI said the model helped identify 81 previously unknown Firefox vulnerabilities that Mozilla classified as high severity and built exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including 588 previously unknown ones, plus disclosed 304 critical Linux findings to maintainers. The company cited rising attempts by malicious cyber actors to misuse AI.
items.title: OpenAI Rates GPT-6 Cyber as Critical for Security

items.summary: This week's VoxDevTalks episode highlights several studies in development economics, covering supply chains, economic inclusion, manufacturing and growth models. Researchers found that India's COVID-era supply chains held up when built on complex inputs; Ugandan people with disabilities participate 18–20% less in economic activity despite an inclusive programme improving their livelihoods but not community attitudes; most Indian manufacturing workers are in small firms, explaining around 40% of the firm-size gap between poorer and richer states; and a career guidance workshop raised high school enrolment in rural Cambodia for over three years. Tim Besley discusses state capacity clusters, while Michael Peters examines service-led growth.
items.title: This week in development economics at VoxDev: 06/11/2026

items.summary: A half-day career guidance workshop built around a personalised app raised high school enrolment and completion among grade 9 students in rural Cambodia, with gains lasting more than three years. The study randomly assigned schools to treatment or control groups (Gehrke, Lenel, and Schupp forthcoming), following 1,715 students through official records plus a phone survey conducted about five months after the workshop during COVID-19 lockdowns. Treated students scored higher on their grade 9 final exam and were more likely to enrol in high school, progress further, sit midterms, and complete secondary schooling roughly 3.5 years later. Gains concentrated among stronger students; weaker ones may have aligned aspirations with vocational routes. The authors note the workshop cost about US$7 per student and offer lessons for scaling guidance without reproducing inequalities.
items.title: Low-Cost Career Workshop Boosts High School Enrolment in Cambodia

items.summary: Anthropic faces lower initial public offering valuations following a steep AI-stock decline, with prospective buyers discussing $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, according to Bloomberg. Some investors previously cited up to $2 trillion in early October. The Nasdaq fell 6.4% on Thursday, erasing $2.3 trillion of market capitalization and setting a one-session record. Anthropic's amended Form S-1 reported $33.24 billion revenue for January through September with a net loss; its last funding round valued it at $965 billion.
items.title: Anthropic IPO valuation expectations fall after AI stock selloff

items.summary: IT services company Coforge entered a strategic partnership with SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI), joining its Partner Network as a Transformation Partner. The collaboration focuses on helping businesses integrate and deploy the Grok portfolio across enterprise operations, with solutions tailored to individual requirements and designed to deliver measurable outcomes.
items.title: Coforge Joins SpaceX Super Intelligence Network for Grok AI Deployment

items.summary: CEO Elon Musk said Tesla will phase out Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to expand Cybercab output. He stated the truck sold 70,000 units over three years with a net project loss of $1.9 billion against $2 billion in research and development spending. The move reflects Tesla's broader shift toward artificial intelligence and robotics as it axed other models this year.
items.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production for Cybercab Expansion

items.summary: Three House Republican committee chairs asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to brief them behind closed doors on his reported relationship with Alice Huang, an executive accused of passing information to Chinese intelligence. The letter requests a November 18 meeting before Nvidia's third-quarter earnings report. Trump was reportedly briefed but took no action. Megaspeed and Nvidia say the interactions were not unusual and allege no wrongdoing.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Asked To Brief Congress Over Alleged China Ties

items.summary: India's IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the government's semiconductor and manufacturing schemes will prioritise serious, technologically capable players with long-term commitments. Coinciding with the Friday launch of the Semicon 2.0 web application portal for machines, fabs and packaging applications, he asked the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme Secretary to reject about 18-19 non-serious applicants already identified. He said only complete applications from value-focused players aligned with Atmanirbhar Bharat would be accepted.
items.title: IT Minister Vaishnaw Demands Long-Term Commitment From Semiconductor Players

items.summary: RW-Voice EQ AS announces a collaboration with Liva AI to add private data covering two new accents, Egyptian and Nigerian English, to the Open ASR Leaderboard. The additions follow earlier splits from Appen and DataOceanAI and Voice Arena. RW-Voice frames the work as part of an effort to improve accent representation in speech-recognition evaluations and reduce benchmark gaming, noting that more accents allow a richer breakdown based on Kachru’s Three Circles model.
items.title: Liva AI Partners to Add Egyptian and Nigerian Accents to Open ASR Leaderboard

items.summary: The Election Commission announced on Friday that voters excluded from draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision exercise in seven states—Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland—will get another opportunity to be included in final rolls. Those marked Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate need not submit Form-8 if they have moved residence; instead they should submit an enumeration form with Annexure-C stating the new address. Officials will also set up a monitoring mechanism to prevent both denial and duplicate enrolments.
items.title: Election Commission Offers Second Chance for Excluded Voters

items.summary: On Dhanteras, Indian jewellery and metal stocks rose amid improving market sentiment, with Titan Company rebounding 3. 5% from its day's low while Kalyan Jewellers gained 5%. The rally follows strong earnings by Titan and a second consecutive session of gains for the Sensex and Nifty. Axis Securities notes gold has corrected more than 20% from its peak, setting an upside target of Rs 1,50,000 per 10 grams with support at Rs 1,21,000; Religare Broking recommends accumulation in silver within the Rs 1,50,000-Rs 1,63,000 per kg range.
items.title: Dhanteras lifts gold stocks as brokers see value in correction

items.summary: The Hong Kong High Court sentenced Joshua Wong Chi-fung on November 5, 2026 to a 10-year prison term for conspiring with foreign forces under the National Security Law. The ruling treats his conduct as one continuing offense spanning multiple acts aimed at endangering national security. Earlier convictions include an 56-month sentence in November 2024 for conspiracy to subvert state power, and involvement in the 2019 protests against extradition amendments. Author Kong Qingjiang of CGTN argues that freedom must operate within legal boundaries and warns that those who threaten national security face accountability as Hong Kong moves toward stability.
items.title: Hong Kong Court Sentences Joshua Wong To Ten Years

items.summary: The Indian stock market will hold a one-hour Muhurat Trading session on Sunday from 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm, with the pre-open period running earlier. The exchanges detailed order-entry windows, limit-order rules and closing auctions across that window. MCX’s special commodity session runs separately until 2:19 pm. The market will next close on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada. Article writer Debaroti Adhikary is not a SEBI-registered analyst or adviser, and views are those of the original research report only.
items.title: Indian Exchanges Set Muhurat Trading and Diwali Closure Times for 2026

items.summary: Xiamen's World Ocean Week offered the public a rare chance to climb inside a full-scale simulator of China's Jiaolong manned submersible. The event featured CGTN's Liu Jiaxin, who took a simulated dive with a real pilot to experience 7,000-meter pressure firsthand. Jiaolong is China's first operational deep-sea manned submersible, designed for depths up to 7,000 meters.
items.title: Public Simulated Dive Inside China's Jiaolong Submersible

items.summary: The article presents Xiamen, called the "Garden City" in Southeast China, as a place known for beautiful seascapes and green spaces where wildlife thrive. It describes how the city has developed its ecological reputation over decades of consistent environmental action, then invites readers to explore what it calls an inspiring story about the region's natural beauty and long-standing commitment to protecting it.
items.title: Xiamen Showcases Its Green City Legacy Through Environmental Storytelling

items.summary: China's top legislature adopted a law on Friday to prevent and punish cross-border corruption. Passed at a session of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, it aims to deepen international anti-corruption cooperation while safeguarding China's sovereignty, security and development interests. The law contains 47 articles across six chapters covering mechanisms, case handling and legal liability.
items.title: China Adopts Law Against Cross-Border Corruption

items.summary: Chinese scientists cooled a cloud of rubidium atoms aboard China's space station to an equivalent temperature of 9.7 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero, described by the research team as a record low. The findings were published in Science and used the ultracold atom physics facility in the Mengtian laboratory module. Researchers observed the cloud expansion for seven seconds after release, which could support quantum experiments and precision measurements. Wolfgang Ketterle noted that on Earth the cloud would fall about 250 meters before crashing to the ground.
items.title: Chinese Team Sets Atomic Cooling Record on Space Station

items.summary: After researcher Mrinank Sharma resigned from Anthropic and posted a widely viewed letter warning of an “in peril” world, white-collar professionals across tech, public relations, consulting and other fields say AI has altered their work. Some have left entirely for careers such as teaching, policing or acting; others pursue additional degrees or freelance streams to feel more secure. Economic data from the Economist shows AI created about 1m US jobs versus 200,000 layoffs attributed to it, yet a Pew Research Center survey found 71% of Americans expect fewer jobs over 20 years. University of Notre Dame economics professor Brendan Moore says fears may stem more from tech leaders’ warnings than from data, though he warns mass resignations could still affect wages and growth.
items.title: White-collar workers quit jobs amid AI fears

items.summary: A Macao court sentenced former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San, 69, to 12½ years in prison Friday in the region's first national security case after a closed-door trial. He was found guilty of subverting state power, breaching confidentiality and contacting overseas groups between 2023 and 2024, including leaking confidential gaming-license information as a lawmaker in 2021. The secrecy drew concerns about fairness from critics like Portuguese lawyer Jorge Menezes, who said Au did not plead guilty. His wife Virginia Cheang called it groundless persecution, while the Macao government backed the ruling and urged respect for national security law enforcement.
items.title: Macao Sentences Ex-Lawmaker in First National Security Case

items.summary: The U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, according to a Labor Department report released Friday. The job market picked up steam last month while the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1% from 4.2% the previous month. Industries adding jobs included health care, manufacturing, and business services, while restaurants and construction cut positions. Average wages rose 3.1% year over year, though an Indeed economist said workers remain losing ground as inflation climbed to 3.7% in September.
items.title: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October as unemployment fell

items.summary: A Kenyan court sentenced doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie to a total of 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one children. Justice Diana Mochache found him guilty after ruling he bore the primary criminal culpability for instructing followers to fast to death so they could meet Jesus. Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, which she declined despite meeting its threshold, citing no prospect of rehabilitation. Mackenzie was tried with 28 accomplices who received sentences up to 160 years. The convictions cover only 191 victims while more than 400 bodies were exhumed from Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast.
items.title: Kenyan Court Sentences Doomsday Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie to Life

items.summary: Czech arms maker Czechoslovak Group (CSG) announced in mid-October that it has acquired a stake in Canadian space technology manufacturer MDA Space. The deal is part of the company's bid to continue riding the defense boom driven by Russia's war in Ukraine, which expanded CZ sector exports from €600 million in 2021 to €4.7 billion in 2025. CSG estimates global government spending on space defense reached €65.83 billion last year and that the overall space economy will triple to €1.6 trillion over the next decade, though it frames these as company estimates.
items.title: Czech CSG Buys Space Tech Firm Amid Arms Boom

items.summary: A federal judge has temporarily blocked construction of President Trump's 250-foot arch in Washington, D.C., with District Court Judge Tanya Chutkan halting work for 14 days at the request of D.C. and Virginia governments. NPR's Rachel Treisman reports that a National Capital Planning Commission filled with Trump allies approved the project despite significant opposition. Separately, the Labor Department is set to release its latest jobs report; NPR's Scott Horsley says it may show employers added about 60,000 jobs last month. The newsletter also covers school enrollment declines and health claims about fluoride alternatives.
items.title: Judge Halts Trump's Arch; Labor Department Set to Release Jobs Report

items.summary: Many Zambians seek civil service careers for its stability, but recent retirements, dismissals and restructuring across public institutions have unsettled that perception. Affected staff include former police officer Godfrey Chilabi, dismissed in October; deputy inspector general Charity Munganga; and all Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency workers following an audit reset. ZEMA directors were placed on administrative leave pending assessment. The changes sparked parliamentary debate after the August 2026 election, with opposition lawmakers led by Stephen Kampyongo questioning transparency amid high living costs.
items.title: Zambia's Civil Service Overhaul Raises Questions About Fairness and Transparency

items.summary: The Indicator from Planet Money reports that gold dropped below $4,000 per ounce this week after reaching nearly $5,600 in January. Co-host Jeff Guo says the main driver is rising Treasury bond yields, which offer income and act as an inflation hedge—advantages gold lacks since it earns no interest. While geopolitical tension from the Iran war could push investors toward safe havens, its effect so far has mainly raised oil prices, pushing rates up and making bonds more attractive than gold. The newsletter notes economic uncertainty remains but does not attribute a single cause definitively to one factor beyond yields.
items.title: Indicator explains why gold prices fell below $4,000

items.summary: Japan's population is falling, especially in rural areas, yet abandoned farms are also losing wildlife rather than gaining it. A 2025 study from Japan found biodiversity stayed stable only where the human population did; elsewhere butterflies, fireflies, frogs, birds and native plants declined. Nature reports that humans had shaped these mosaic landscapes for species to depend on. Adam Spitzig of Stanford University said small farms can boost biodiversity while supporting food production.
items.title: Abandoned Japanese Farms Lose Wildlife as Villages Empty

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV departed Friday for his first trip to the Americas since being elected in May 2025, traveling through November 17. He will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru but not the United States, declining a White House invitation tied to the July 4 Declaration of Independence anniversary.
