The itinerary emphasizes coexistence and unity amid regional polarization, though his message on social justice may clash with governments aligned with President Trump. His health is under scrutiny after lung-tumor surgery in October; Vatican sources say he needs no special measures. Heavy El Niño rains have triggered emergencies across northern Peru ahead of large gatherings.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV's First Americas Trip Under Trump's Shadow

items.summary: Ravi Uppal, co-founder of the Mahadev betting app and one of its main promoters alongside Sourabh Chandrakar, was arrested in Dubai. The Enforcement Directorate and Central Bureau of Investigation are working to bring him back to India at the earliest, per news agency ANI. An Interpol Red Corner Notice had been issued against Uppal in October 2023; he was detained in December that year but released after 45 days. The ED alleges he oversaw a hawala network with transactions worth hundreds of crores and facilitated movement of funds into India, while also accusing him of links to Chhattisgarh politicians and bureaucrats. In January 2026 the agency attached assets worth approximately ₹21 crore linked to him. Both men reportedly hold Vanuatu passports used to evade Indian agencies; Vanuatu has no extradition treaty with India.
items.title: Mahadev App Co-Founder Ravi Uppal Arrested in Dubai on Hawala Charges

items.summary: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck off the coast of Tokyo on Friday, Japanese authorities said, with no tsunami alert issued. The shallow quake hit at 7:39 pm near Kanto region, and Japan's Meteorological Agency reported seismic intensity 3, meaning almost everyone indoors felt shaking and dishes may rattle. Its epicenter lay about 169 kilometers southeast of Asahi per the US Geological Survey. There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries.
items.title: Magnitude 6.1 Quake Strikes Near Tokyo Without Tsunami Warning

items.summary: The Election Commission said citizens whose names were dropped from draft electoral rolls during the special revision can submit a fresh enumeration form to be added to the final list. The rule applies where forms went missing or people were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate. Booth officers will issue new forms; movers must attach residence proof and need not file Form 8.
items.title: Election Commission lets excluded voters reapply in seven states and territories

items.summary: Kerala-born Nithya Raman won the Los Angeles mayoral race, becoming the first Indian-American and first South Asian elected to lead the city. Incumbent Karen Bass conceded defeat after her term was undermined by the Palisades Fire, making her the first LA mayor in two decades to lose reelection. Raman, an urban planner and Ivy League-educated council member since 2020, campaigned on housing, homelessness and policing reform. She entered as a late entrant who had initially backed Bass before flipping. Her victory means New York and Los Angeles will both have South Asian mayors. The Indian-American community registered broad midterm gains across the country.
items.title: Nithya Raman Wins Los Angeles Mayoral Race as First South Asian Mayor

items.summary: In the midterm elections, voters under 30 showed the sharpest shift toward the Democrats after many had backed Donald Trump in 2024. About seven in ten young voters supported the Democratic candidate for Congress, and roughly six in ten cited opposition to Trump as a reason. The swing was largest among Latino youth, who voted overwhelmingly Democratic, while older groups moved less sharply.
items.title: Young Voters Drove Democratic Midterm Gains

items.summary: Japan convened its first government panel of experts Friday to help draft a plan reversing the country’s declining birthrate and restructuring systems for a shrinking population. Minister Minoru Kiuchi called it “a national crisis that is unfolding quietly.” Japan’s fertility rate was 1.14 last year, the lowest on record, while deaths (766,746) outpaced births (320,458). IPSS projections put the population below 100 million by 2056 and as low as about 80 million by 2070. The panel’s views will inform a strategy due by December.
items.title: Japan convenes expert panel on population decline

items.summary: A wave of student and cost-of-living protests has spread from France to Belgium, Germany, Italy, Spain and Portugal. Some marches turned violent with clashes, looting and destruction, while authorities faced criticism for excessive force and mass arrests. The unrest comes against mounting economic pressure: France's public debt is projected to reach 120 percent of GDP by 2027, and inflation across the EU and eurozone hit 3.8 percent in September, up from 2.1 percent in 2024.
items.title: Student and cost-of-living protests spread across Europe amid economic strain

items.summary: Jean-Luc Melenchon, a hard-left candidate in the upcoming 2027 French presidential election, is popular with young voters but also highly controversial. His support for youth protests has increased his divisiveness ahead of the vote. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young supporters to explore why he remains favored by Gen Z.
items.title: Why Jean-Luc Melenchon Appeals to French Gen Z Voters

items.summary: India Today Digital's ground check at Sadar Bazar found illegal and uncertified firecrackers on sale despite the Supreme Court allowing only certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR. The team observed questionable products, QR codes returning no information, China-made stock with Mandarin labels, and little understanding among sellers of what a green cracker is. Security personnel from Delhi Police, CRPF and CISF were present but seen buying rather than enforcing rules; one advised on transport instead of inspecting goods. A shopkeeper said buyers should rush purchases before police arrive. On Friday morning the city's AQI crossed 700 while enforcement appeared minimal. The Supreme Court order permits certified green crackers only on November 7 and 8 within set hours, but visible compliance was lacking.
items.title: Police Present But Unchecked at Delhi Cracker Market

items.summary: A bipartisan permitting reform bill, BAAJA, faces uncertainty after Democrats won midterm control of Congress. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries opposed the legislation in its current form, citing concerns it revises laws like the National Environmental Policy Act and weakens environmental statutes. Lobbyist Chris Moyer said Democratic leverage has changed his outlook on passing it during the lame-duck session. Analyst Kevin Kircher's report found the bill would raise clean electricity revenue by $2.1 million per life lost to pollution from fossil fuels, below the EPA's roughly $12 million standard. Clean energy groups urge swift passage before Congress ends this year while business and environmental advocates debate trade-offs over accelerating both renewable and fossil fuel projects.
items.title: Democratic Gains Cast Doubt on Energy Permitting Bill

items.summary: Nearly 50 residents gathered in Fairfax, Iowa, to voice anger and fear over a proposed natural gas plant less than three miles from town. Nine months earlier, Interstate Power and Light had abandoned plans after opposition; Alliant Energy then announced land purchase for the site. In October, the Linn County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to reject Alliant's rezoning request, citing water infrastructure gaps and overwhelming community opposition. The Morgan Valley Energy Center would run 1,230 to 3,950 hours yearly. Residents link rising demand from nearby data centers—Google and QTS campuses using combined 1.6 gigawatts—to the need for fossil plants, raising concerns amid Linn County's net-zero goal by 2050 set in 2019. Alliant disputed the rejection; a utilities commission hearing is scheduled next month.
items.title: Iowa Residents Reject Gas Plant Amid Data Center Growth

items.summary: The Supreme Court permitted certified green crackers for Diwali in Delhi NCR on specific dates and times, with a total ban from November 9. Separately, India has improved cyclone disaster preparedness since the 1999 Odisha super cyclone through advanced forecasting models, Doppler radars, satellites, timely warnings enabling large-scale evacuations supported by shelters and coastal barriers. Despite effective emergency responses preventing human loss, challenges remain in restoring livelihoods, homes, and infrastructure after disasters.
items.title: India Strengthens Cyclone Preparedness Since 1999 Odisha Disaster

items.summary: Hindustan Times' evening news brief of November 6 leads with two stories. Delhi-NCR implemented Stage 3 of the Graded Response Action Plan (Grap) after its air quality index reached 382, classified as 'very poor', approaching the 400 mark that would trigger a 'severe' category; the restrictions target dust pollution and emissions across Noida, Ghaziabad and Gurugram. Separately, an FIR into Thursday's Chawri Bazar building collapse in Old Delhi, which killed at least two people, alleges contractors ignored worker warnings about poor construction material and structural weakness.
items.title: HT Evening News Brief November 6: Grap 3 imposed in Delhi, FIR on Chawri Bazar collapse reveals ignored warnings

items.summary: A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software alongside Sionna and other tools aimed at accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Global developer adoption of the AI Aerial and Sionna software has grown 10x over the past year, while the broader toolset surpassed 1 million downloads; more than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide now use them. Researchers report a robot task completion time reduction of up to 52.6% versus periodic images at King’s College London, higher uplink throughput for SoftBank’s neural receiver across all tested settings, and a RAN power consumption cut of 45.6% from the University of Leeds team.
items.title: NVIDIA Open Source Tools Advance 6G Research

items.summary: Google's Data Cloud connectors, now in preview within Gemini, let business users and analysts query live enterprise data using natural language. The feature addresses a common problem: across most organizations, data questions multiply faster than analysts can answer them, stalling projects and spreading unmanaged spreadsheets. Early generative AI tools struggled with accurate SQL generation and governance rules; these connectors resolve governed data directly from the workspace while enforcing row- and column-level security under end-user credentials. Queries run through Knowledge Catalog to map everyday terms into exact database structures, then execute via permission-aware execution using federated query mode without copying or indexing data.
items.title: Data Cloud Connectors Bring Conversational Analytics to Gemini in Preview

items.summary: TikTok owner ByteDance is reportedly considering expanding a data center project in northeastern Brazil, according to Bloomberg News. The report was published on Friday and reflects an ongoing evaluation of the company's plans for its Brazilian operations.
items.title: ByteDance Weighs Data Center Expansion in Brazil

items.summary: Researchers at Check Point Research found that OpenAI's ChatGPT Lockdown Mode, designed to limit prompt-injection risks and data leaks, contained an escape route. Using HTML previews inside code blocks, they opened unrestricted pop-up windows enabling silent chat-data theft, credential phishing and malware delivery through a trusted interface. Eli Smadja of Check Point Research said AI security controls depend on the surrounding application environment. OpenAI removed the sandbox permissions after disclosure; a retest confirmed the method no longer works.
items.title: Check Point finds vulnerability in ChatGPT’s Lockdown Mode

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to make room for the Cybercab robotaxi. The pickup has faced weak sales, with US figures falling 48% in 2025 to 20,237 vehicles per Kelley Blue Book estimates cited by the Associated Press. Musk did not clarify whether production would relocate or end entirely, nor address outstanding orders.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Production Wind-Down in 2027

items.summary:
A Reuters report citing independent researcher Derik Kauffman says Apple keeps an undisclosed multilingual list of roughly 100,000 words that its iPhone keyboard avoids suggesting through predictive text, autocorrect and swipe-typing. Kauffman said most flagged expressions are vulgar or offensive, but the list also excludes politically sensitive phrases about leaders, immigration and territorial disputes, including 'dictator Trump' and 'Tibetan independence.' Apple told Reuters users can still type words manually and override suggestions, describing its keyboard as designed to avoid inappropriate language. Kauffman called it a light-touch form of censorship with large impact at scale, while questioning the filtering's consistency, noting phrases like 'read gay smut' were restricted even when similar ones were not. Reuters independently tested several expressions and found them difficult or impossible to enter via swipe-typing or autocomplete.

items.summary: Shiv Sena minister Sanjay Shirsat alleged on Friday that AIMIM state president Imtiaz Jaleel had been named a prime accused in the Nashik Tata Consultancy Services case involving alleged sexual harassment and religious conversion. Shirsat claimed Jaleel arranged shelter for key accused Nida Khan, who stayed 35 days with relatives, and that voice samples matched recordings linked to the case. Jaleel confirmed being made a co-accused but said he was unaware of the charges; TCS maintained its zero-tolerance policy on harassment.
items.title: Shiv Sena Minister Accuses AIMIM Leader of Sheltering TCS Nashik Case Accused

items.summary: A researcher named Derek Kauffman reported discovering an undisclosed list of roughly 100,000 multilingual terms that Apple's iOS keyboard omits from predictive and swipe-typing features. Reuters said the list contains vulgar, drug-, sex- and violence-related words plus politically sensitive phrases such as 'dictator Trump' and 'sleepy Joe.' Kauffman called it a light-touch censorship whose scale could produce large effects. He estimated around 100,000 entries excluding Chinese characters; Reuters independently corroborated findings with swipe-typing tests on United Ireland and Sleepy Joe.
items.title: Researcher Reveals Apple's Hidden Word Graylist

items.summary:
A new Ramp report finds that although companies are using more AI than ever, their spending on it has flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose. According to Ramp's data, token spend grew only 1. 5% across August and September, compared with 42% in July. Ramp lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch that almost all AI spend comes from venture-backed tech firms, so a slowdown among the top cohort could trigger cascading effects despite rising volumes. He attributes the trend to price cuts by OpenAI and Anthropic and growing customer thriftiness rather than weak demand. The report arrives as Bloomberg reported Anthropic's potential valuation fell sharply before its IPO. Kharazian cautioned that assumptions about sustained hypergrowth may be breaking down, though he noted a re-acceleration in October data remains possible.

items.title: Ramp Data Signals AI Spending Slowdown Ahead of Anthropic IPO

items.summary: The International Energy Agency said in its Renewables 2026 report that global renewable capacity is expected to grow by almost 4,800 gigawatts over the 2026-2031 period. The agency attributed faster deployment to energy security concerns and rising fuel prices following a Strait of Hormuz crisis. Emerging markets outside China are set to match advanced economies for the first time.
items.title: IEA Forecasts Nearly 4,800 GW of New Renewables by 2031 Amid Energy Security Push

items.summary: A November roundup reports job cuts at several large tech firms just before the holiday season. The companies named are Amazon, Angi, Block, Canva, and Squarespace. For Amazon specifically, a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notice filed with Washington state indicates about 95 employees will be separated from employment in the state; Amazon described this as “approximately 95 employees will be separated from employment with Amazon.” The notice lists affected roles including managers, software developers, engineers, and more. These WARN layoffs follow workers notified in October, adding to over 30,000 Amazon layoffs in the past year.
items.title: Tech Layoffs Hit Amazon, Angi, Block, Canva and Squarespace Before Holidays

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Apple will begin monitoring public iCloud links for harmful content starting with iOS 27.3, affecting only links marked “Anyone with the Link.” The company says it may block or disable accounts and involve law enforcement if policy is violated, but did not define what constitutes harmful content. Limited-access links remain encrypted and unmonitored. Apple also notes an appeals framework exists for false flags.
items.title: Apple Begins Monitoring Public iCloud Links in iOS 27.3

items.summary: In the third quarter, Alphabet built a stake worth nearly $548 million in longtime partner Qualcomm as it expands into data centers amid a smartphone downturn. Qualcomm shares rose 3 per cent premarket after tumbles earlier. The chipmaker expects its data-center revenue to reach $15 billion by 2029 and has secured orders from Amazon, Microsoft and Meta.
items.title: Alphabet Builds $548 Million Stake in Qualcomm Amid Data Center Push

items.summary: India's passenger vehicle market shows strong festive demand around Dhanteras and Diwali, with some makers struggling over inventory limits. Maruti Suzuki India expects about 30,000 vehicles on Dhanteras; Hyundai Motor India targets roughly 16,000 across the two days, nearly 14% higher than last year; Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles anticipates single-day deliveries crossing 12,000 units. Mahindra faces tight SUV stocks and capacity constraints as demand outpaces supply.
items.title: Indian automakers forecast strong Dhanteras deliveries amid tight stock

items.summary: Tribal activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat allegedly died by suicide in Ranchi on Friday, hanging from a ceiling fan at her residence. Police said prima facie she took her own life after going live on Facebook and accusing the Hemant Soren government and land brokers of harassing her; the exact reason is yet to be ascertained. The nearly 11-minute video cuts off with the camera obstructed by a green object.
items.title: Jharkhand tribal activist dies by suicide after Facebook Live

items.summary: On Friday, Amazon announced a new feature letting customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to shop on the platform. The rollout targets select U.S. customers just before holiday shopping begins and can be expanded in coming weeks via waitlist signups. Users may search, add items to cart, purchase, compare products, upload images for similar listings, track prices, manage lists, and check order status.
items.title: Amazon launches text-based Alexa shopping feature ahead of holidays

items.summary: Veeam warned customers that its Software Appliance virtual machines can intermittently fail to boot and crash with a kernel panic after rebooting, including reboots following updates. The company said the issue stems from an early-boot FIPS-mode jitterentropy health test in the appliance's Linux kernel failing on certain AMD EPYC processors, such as 7262, 7302, and 7F72. Veeam noted affected systems show a specific kernel panic error message. It advised redeploying to an unaffected processor or disabling automatic updates.
items.title: Veeam Warns of Boot Failures on AMD EPYC Hosts

items.summary: OpenAI's chief financial officer Sarah Friar told CNBC on Friday that the company will continue spending on AI computing capacity, even though Tuesday's midterm elections saw voters back limits on data centers in local ballot measures.
items.title: OpenAI CFO Vows Data Center Spending After Election Rebuke

items.summary: In The Blueprint, Mito's CEO Iñaki Berenguer and Head of Engineering Keyvan Akbary describe building an orchestration platform on Google Cloud to produce a 120-second national TV spot for Movistar Plus+, part of Telefónica, airing across Spain during the World Cup. For Movistar alone, they generated over 5000 assets (1000 videos) in around 65 iteration rounds, exposing bottlenecks in asset management, collaboration, rendering latency and model consistency. Their serverless architecture uses Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Vertex AI and a Rule of 6 to enable real-time collaboration and cost efficiency. The production team describes the resulting campaign as 95% AI-generated, with 1,441 assets live on a shared Canvas near launch. The spot follows Tommy, a 17-year-old student making an AI video project.
items.title: Mito Orchestrates Thousands of AI Assets for a World Cup TV Spot

items.summary: US payrolls rose by 165,000 in October after a revised September gain of 60,000, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labour Statistics said on Nov 6. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Reuters economists had forecast gains of 65,000. Professional and business services led with 70,000 jobs added. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% over the past 12 months, still behind inflation.
items.title: US October Payrolls Beat Forecasts as Unemployment Drops

items.summary: Sony Group introduced a US$60 (S$77) wired headphone model, the MDR-3R, styled after 1979 Walkman-era headphones but updated with USB-C connectivity and an in-line microphone. The company said it kept the original's 23mm drivers for similar sound while adding subtle refinements to suit modern listening.
items.title: Sony Launches Retro-Styled Wired Headphones at $60

items.summary: Databricks presents Unity Gateway as a way for public sector organizations to govern artificial intelligence at scale, building on existing data governance rather than adding separate infrastructure. The piece argues that agencies handle sensitive citizen and defense information, so compliance requirements are mandatory; without answers to cost, access, and where requests are processed, projects stall. It describes how the tool lets teams control which models and agents run for each mission, set spending limits by user or team, apply platform-level content guardrails, route tasks through more cost-effective models via Smart Routing, and require that foundation-model requests be processed within a workspace's geography. Unity Gateway is built into Databricks so administrators can manage access without deploying an external solution.
items.title: Unity Gateway Brings AI Governance To Public Sector

items.summary: Anthropic has introduced a Personal Finance feature that lets users connect their bank and credit card accounts to its AI assistant Claude. The tool answers spending questions in everyday language, breaking down expenses, flagging missed payments, and estimating remaining funds before payday. It analyses financial information only and is not designed to handle money or make investment decisions.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Personal Finance Feature to Claude for Spending Analysis

items.summary: Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, asked home minister Amit Shah to persuade Prime Minister Narendra Modi to hold a debate on special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls. He shared a video showing Shah contradicting his own remarks during parliamentary discussion and urged him not to 'confuse' the prime minister with such statements.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Urges Shah To Convince Modi For SIR Debate

items.summary: The European Commission launched a WTO safeguard investigation into certain PET resin chemicals, notified under G/SG/N/6/EU/5. The inquiry examines whether increased imports are causing or threatening serious injury to the domestic industry. Interested parties may submit questionnaires within 21 days of initiation and request hearings in the same period; written representations must be filed by the stated deadlines.
items.title: EU launches safeguard investigation into PET resin chemicals

items.summary: Speculation is growing over a possible power struggle in Maharashtra’s Nationalist Congress Party, which split into two factions in 2023. Nephew Rohit Pawar warned relatives Sunetra Pawar and her sons to understand BJP strategies, while senior leaders reportedly met Union home minister Amit Shah, though the NCP spokesperson Umesh Patil denied it as “completely incorrect.” The buzz follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s message of support for hospitalised Sharad Pawar. The party has denied all speculations of any power tussle within the party. Analysts suggest BJP may seek to co-opt Sharad Pawar’s political infrastructure, with possible cabinet gains and opposition realignment at stake.
items.title: NCP Factions Face Possible Political Churn Amid Modi-Pawar Overtures

items.summary: The EU's diplomatic position at next week's COP31 summit in Antalya is complicated by a domestic political retreat on climate policy and rising global opposition to its carbon border tax, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). India has hardened its stance: Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said New Delhi will defend industrial interests against what he called unilateral trade barriers, while Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal warned CBAM could raise import duties. The EU's CBAM took effect in January 2026 and covers aluminum, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, iron and steel. Canada, the United States, the UK and Russia have all sought exemptions or raised disputes, with Russia and China announcing joint opposition on 3 November. Meanwhile, EU co-legislators are set to meet on 20 November as Brussels weighs extending CBAM to washing machines and car parts amid pressure over energy prices and industrial concerns.
items.title: EU Climate Tax Risks Trade War With India at COP31

items.summary: As India and the US work to finalise a long-awaited trade deal, Republicans' loss in the November 3 midterms has raised questions about how the shift affects negotiations. Experts offer differing views: Professor Rituparna Kaushik of FLAME University said results would not rewrite US policy overnight because Section 301 and Section 232 duties rest on executive authority facing a presidential veto, though a Democratic Congress may give India room to negotiate on substance. Ajay Srivastava of the Global Trade Research Initiative expects Trump to fast-track an early agreement amid domestic constraints, yet warned protectionism would remain largely unchanged. For 2025, goods exports reached $103.82 billion from India and about $45.6 billion from the US, with total bilateral trade at $149.42 billion; services trade hit $92.23 billion. A final deal remains elusive amid a Section 301 probe and threats of tariffs around 17-19 per cent linked to Russian oil purchases.
items.title: US midterm losses may reshape India-US trade talks

items.summary: US stocks recovered on Wall Street following the market's most severe single-day drop in nearly two years, driven by renewed optimism over a strong jobs report. The Nasdaq rose 1.2% while tech names like Nvidia and AMD led gains; the Dow fell about 1%. European markets had tumbled overnight after Democrats won the midterms, sparking AI-industry slowdown worries.
items.title: Wall Street rebounds after worst day in 19 months amid AI-slowdown fears

items.summary: Feature Views, a capability of Databricks Feature Store, let teams define each ML feature once so the same definition produces point-in-time training data and managed pipelines for online inference. The walkthrough follows a $900 payment through Kafka to a Model Serving endpoint that returns fraud_probability and fraud_prediction. Real-time detection must weigh recent activity, longer-term baselines such as a 30-day average and standard deviation, and the current request amount; one customer's $900 sits six standard deviations above their mean while another's sits only one above theirs. A single definition prevents data leakage from future transactions and training-serving skew between offline scoring and live inference. The design is governed by Unity Catalog for permissions and lineage, with feature privileges controlling registration, reading and materialization.
items.title: Databricks Feature Views unify fraud model training and live scoring

items.summary: A fresh wave of bomb threats disrupted at least 18 flights on Friday, affecting airports and airspace in Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, France, Hungary, Italy, Portugal, Romania and the UK. Searches found no explosive devices and all aircraft landed safely. The alerts followed separate warnings on Tuesday and Thursday that forced at least 35 flights to be diverted or searched, raising questions over an apparently coordinated effort to cause chaos for travellers. Officials described it as a possible hybrid aggression campaign targeting civilian infrastructure, while investigators reported no evidence of state sponsorship.
items.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe amid coordinated-attack fears

items.summary: Shares of TD Power and Thermax fell about 15% each, while HFCL and Sterlite Technologies hit the lower circuit on a broad Indian tech rout. The decline followed concerns that Democratic gains in the US midterm elections could restrict data centre expansion and slow AI infrastructure development. A sharp technology sell-off erased roughly $2.5 trillion from US markets, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping 5.52% to close at 24,315, its steepest single-day fall since April 2025. The rout spread across Asia as investors de-risked amid uncertainty over AI spending and valuation resets.
items.title: Indian stocks fall as global AI selloff deepens amid US election fears

items.summary: In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 1,800 votes with roughly 96% of ballots counted. Under state law allowing late mail-in ballots, the Associated Press has not called the contest and a final result may not arrive until early next week.
items.title: Mississippi Senate Race Remains Uncalled as Democrats Chase Blue Wave

items.summary: Global tech stocks fell sharply following the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, with concerns about a slowdown in artificial intelligence development. Major corporations including Apple, Tesla and Nvidia lost around $1tn during one trading session. Reporters question whether this reflects market volatility or signals that an AI bubble may be close to bursting.
items.title: Tech stocks plunge amid fears of AI bubble burst after Democrats' midterms sweep

items.summary: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms rose on Friday as markets recovered from a rout that wiped trillions off values, beginning Thursday in the US before spreading to Asia and Europe. Investors had sold AI shares partly over fears that Democrats' control of both houses could slow development through new rules. The Nasdaq Composite flattened around 1.7% higher by lunchtime after its 5.5% fall, while Nvidia gained about 4%. Asian and European markets fared worse, with South Korea's Kospi down 6%. Strong US jobs figures added context: employers added 165,000 jobs in October, above expectations, and unemployment eased to 4.1%, though the rate had held near that range since March. Analysts noted uncertainty over whether the rebound would hold next week.
items.title: AI stocks rebound after midterm-driven tech selloff

items.summary: The Mission Trinity Foodbank in Goole has closed after 16 years, citing rising costs and falling donations. Founder David Sample said funds had declined to the point where they could no longer afford to continue, worsened by the cost of living crisis. The charity bought food up to three times weekly despite reduced donations and supported about 50-60 families each week until January.
items.title: East Yorkshire foodbank closes after 16 years amid rising costs

items.summary: Chinese scientists aboard China's space station cooled a cloud of rubidium atoms to an equivalent temperature of 9.7 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero, described as a record low by the research team. The result was published in Science and used the ultracold atom physics facility in the Mengtian laboratory module. The reported figure characterizes the atoms' slow expansion rather than any surrounding equipment reaching that temperature. Researchers observed cloud expansion for seven seconds after release, enabling longer experiments into quantum behavior and precision measurements.
items.title: Chinese Scientists Set Atomic Cooling Record on Space Station

items.summary: China launched satellites 07-09 of the Yaogan-51 group from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center in Sichuan Province on November 5, 2026. The launch occurred at 11:58 p.m. Beijing Time aboard a Long March-2C carrier rocket and reached its preset orbits successfully. The satellites are used for scientific experiments and electromagnetic environment detection. This was the 675th mission of the Long March rockets.
items.title: China Launches Yaogan-51 Remote Sensing Satellites

items.summary: Investors are weighing whether Democratic control of Congress could burst the AI bubble, after steep falls on world stock markets and a sharp Nasdaq sell-off following mid-term elections that gave Democrats full congressional control. Fears have grown that leading Democrats' campaigns against data-centre expansion will bring more regulation; a Gallup poll in May found 71% would oppose a local data centre versus 53% for a nuclear station. The AI boom, sparked by Open AI's Chat GPT release in late 2022, is expected to reach $1trillion in investments in 2026 alone per Goldman Sachs. Analysts remain divided on whether the drop signals an overvalued market or simply froth being removed.
items.title: US Midterm Wins Spark AI Stock Sell-off

items.summary: In The Vergecast episode titled 'Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election,' Nilay Patel argues that AI products are not good enough to justify their costs. He contends the benefits of features like AI overviews and agents are not real, deep fake content is low quality, data center noise burdens residents, companies spend more than they earn, blood-storage refrigerators in Europe have been hacked, and ties these costs to corruption involving CEOs in Washington.
items.title: Nilay Patel says Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election

items.summary: On Friday (Nov 6), bomb threats warning 'the clock is ticking' were sent to television stations across Europe, prompting evacuations and suspensions of programming. Irish broadcaster RTE, Britain's Sky, Bulgarian station Nova TV and others reported the alerts; no bombs were found at any site. The emails, signed by a purported leader claiming responsibility for recent flight hoaxes, used the name Mikhail Andropov. Their authorship remains unclear, with uncertainty about possible Russian involvement or an attempt to implicate Moscow.
items.title: Bomb Threat Emails Disrupt European TV Channels Amid Broader Hoax Wave

items.summary: Researchers in Canada captured images of an unidentified baby North Atlantic right whale off Anticosti Island in Quebec in September, one of the rarest sea mammals globally. Scientists with the New England Aquarium in Boston said after analyzing photos and data that it was a calf likely born months ago during winter surveys when the animals went unseen.
items.title: Scientists Identify Baby Right Whale Off Canada

items.summary: European officials reported a fresh wave of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, following several hoaxes that caused flight diversions earlier in the week. No suspicious items were found and no one was injured, though authorities noted minimal disruption to aviation across the continent, according to Eurocontrol. The authority said it recorded 14 threatened flights Thursday — only 0.05% of nearly 26,300 daily flights — plus seven on Tuesday. Incidents spanned Hungary, France and Prague's Vaclav Havel Airport, where nine flights were affected. No clear evidence has emerged about who is behind the threats, which come amid warnings that Russia may be ramping up hybrid attacks in Europe. Broadcasters including Ireland's RTE also received security threats.
items.title: Bomb threats target European air traffic amid hoaxes

items.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) released the subject-wise date sheet for its Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations in 2027. Both levels begin on February 16, with all papers starting at 10:30 am; Class 10 ends March 9 and Class 12 concludes April 9. The board said more than 26.5 lakh students registered for Class 10 while over 19.8 lakh are expected in Class 12, and it considered more than 40,000 subject combinations to avoid clashes.
items.title: CBSE Releases Class 10 and 12 Exam Schedule for 2027

items.summary: British comedian Russell Brand was found guilty by a London jury on November 5, 2014, of rape and three sexual assaults. The verdict included charges involving a 16-year-old girl. Judge stated he now faces significant prison time.
items.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Three Sexual Assaults

items.summary: A Ukrainian drone team from the 140th Intelligence Battalion of the Ukrainian Marines, led by Snake and including chief pilot Shamil (33), operates the Baton attack drone to contest Russia’s presence on the left bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region. The unit launches the craft—costing around $3,300 to produce—from a concealed catapult near trees, steering it live from an underground position while its camera feed goes dark moments before impact. Snake frames the conflict as “a war of drone pilots,” noting that since 2022 Ukraine has shifted from a 20th-century to a 21st-century war. Analyst Petro Kobernyk warns that Russian control of the river could enable further advances into Mykolaiv and Odessa, though he doubts Moscow currently lacks resources for another assault on Kherson.
items.title: Ukrainian drone unit contests Russian hold of the Dnipro

items.summary: Obbe Vermeij, a former Rockstar tech director who left in 2009, told Rock Paper Shotgun that an AI-assisted decompilation port of GTA VI could pressure the developer to release its official PC version sooner. He recalled how console fans of the original game resented being given far fewer colors than PC players received. Vermeij noted the long-standing awkward relationship between PC and console releases at Rockstar, where ports often lagged years behind.
items.title: Ex-GTA Tech Director Says AI Clones May Speed Official PC Port

items.summary: A Kenyan High Court in Mombasa sentenced Pastor Paul Mackenzie, leader of the Good News International Church, to 200 years in prison on Friday. He was convicted of murdering 191 people after ordering followers to fast to death. Justice Diana Kavedza found him guilty of relocating members and causing their deaths. Prosecutors sought the death penalty; his lawyer has launched an appeal.
items.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years for mass killings

items.summary: An author reports that AI labs are paying companies large one-time fees for copies of their internal work records—emails, documents, chat logs—to train models. Pitches cited include Wired payments reported at $350K–$1.8M and a possible $2 million raise by another emailer; an entrepreneur friend noted spending over $45B on private data. Startups like Handshake license professional documents across fields including journalism and graduate coursework, while Mercor and Micro1 lead the boom. One founder claims labs pay about $40–$50 billion a year for such data. Privacy critics warn anonymization may not fully remove personal information, citing Spirit Airlines’ sale of 80,000 email accounts amid union objections; Google bid $10 million before Micro1 topped it by $2.5 million. The author declined to sell WIRED’s editorial records.
items.title: AI Firms Race to Buy Workers' Private Work Files

items.summary: Professor Amanda Ellison of Durham University, author of Splitting, explains that the appeal of quick fixes for migraines needs evidence before it becomes reliable advice. She describes how prodrome symptoms like yawning and food cravings can make chocolate seem to trigger attacks when it merely reflects an early phase; a review found insufficient evidence to recommend avoiding it. Caffeine has a legitimate place in some headache medicines, per a Cochrane review, though fast-food meals cannot be treated as remedies. Cooling offers short-term relief but not spoon-level certainty. Established options include triptans and CGRP-targeting preventives. She recommends keeping a headache diary to spot patterns rather than assuming unfamiliar symptoms are migraine.
items.title: A neuroscientist weighs which migraine remedies actually work

items.summary: US authorities have charged Thomas Markle, Meghan Markle's father, with possessing child pornography, alleging he kept images of himself with prepubescent girls. FBI agents searched his Florida aged-care home on Friday; he is expected in Tampa court later that day. The Justice Department says the material was stored in two Los Angeles-area units for nearly two decades. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said they will prosecute to the fullest extent of federal law, and FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed the arrest.
items.title: Meghan Markle's father charged with possessing child pornography

items.summary: A 15-month-old elephant calf named Maya was airlifted from Kochi Airport in Kerala to Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat, for specialised medical care. In July 2026 she suffered an accidental fall and could not stand or rise on her own for nearly two months. After the Kerala Forest Department's treatment failed to improve her condition, a Medical Board recommended shifting her; both teams arranged joint care during the flight so she can receive intensive rehabilitation.
items.title: Kerala elephant calf airlifted for specialised care at Vantara

items.summary: In Switzerland, campaigners displayed a 676-square-metre banner near a data centre being developed by STACK Infrastructure. The display showed images of Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos with the slogan 'Big Tech Bros suck our water, electricity, data'. Greenpeace is calling for a nationwide moratorium on new mega data centres until binding regulations protect energy supplies, water resources and public interest.
items.title: Greenpeace Unveils Giant Banner Criticizing Big Tech Data Centres in Switzerland

items.summary: Bhavya Dore reviews Abir Mukherjee's novel The Pinnacle, noting it is his eighth book and the second set in a contemporary setting. George Abercrombie, an American star living in Mumbai, becomes the prime suspect after discovering his wife Sweety Sahota murdered in their luxury high-rise apartment. Published by Harvill Secker at 432 pages for Rs.899, the novel rotates between three points of view and blends intrigue with comedy. Dore praises Mukherjee's trademark drollery but flags historical inaccuracies that undermine verisimilitude before calling it a fun, solid thriller.
items.title: A Reviewer Frames Abir Mukherjee's Mumbai Thriller

items.summary: An article examines France's mounting debt costs amid political instability, arguing that planned school and university funding may exceed available resources. Public debt stands at around 120% of GDP, with interest payments projected to rise from €79 billion in 2026 toward between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030. Economist Friedrich Heinemann warns that rising spreads could trigger a financial crisis unless course correction occurs. Landry Charrier notes many citizens remain insulated from debt consequences, sustaining support for costly party promises. The piece draws on data including Germany's lower ratio and France's negative credit outlook to frame the risk.
items.title: France's Debt Burden and Political Gridlock Threaten Stability

items.summary: Senate Democratic leader Catherine Cortez Masto says a wave of new red-state senators will reshape the caucus by uniting moderates and progressives on core priorities like restoring Obamacare tax credits, cutting tariffs, limiting Trump’s power over ICE, and protecting energy jobs. She told Semafor she expects center and left to align in 2027. The influx follows her behind-the-scenes work as chair of ModSquad, which raised $4 million for Democrats and whose associated PAC spent $18 million nationally, including $3. 5 million in Iowa and nearly $5 million backing centrists in Virginia and Colorado. New senators-elect include Josh Turek, Adam Hamilton, Abdul El-Sayed, Roy Cooper, James Talarico, Peggy Flanagan, Troy Jackson, Chris Pappas, Scott Colom, and Juliana Stratton. The new members will not be sworn in until next year, but decisions await during the lame duck session on permitting reform and a potential government funding deal.
items.title: Cortez Masto Sees Red-State Democrats Uniting Party Center and Left

items.summary: In Edmunds’ EV Range test, the 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive drove 436 miles on a single charge, topping its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles. Powered by an 800V system and a 108.7 kWh battery, it also used less energy than advertised—28.3 vs. 32 kWh per 100 miles. Edmunds calls it the longest-range luxury EV SUV tested so far.
items.title: BMW iX3 Beats Its Own EPA Range Rating in Real-World Test

items.summary: Europe is advancing a push for technological sovereignty as artificial intelligence grows, though an AI system built entirely on European technology remains impossible given reliance on U.S. chips from Nvidia alone. The most critical dimension lies in where data is stored and processed; many companies now resist sending sensitive information to the servers of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or Microsoft. Charles Sansbury, chief executive of Cloudera, notes that businesses increasingly prefer private clouds or local servers. Marjorie Janiewicz of Mistral says enriching models with proprietary data preserves a competitive edge. A Cloudera report based on surveys of more than 1,500 technology leaders worldwide found nearly half have moved part of their AI operations to private systems.
items.title: European Firms Seek Data Control Amid AI Sovereignty Push

items.summary: Qatar's sovereign wealth fund and Brookfield are backing a proposed 1-gigawatt data center in northern England, potentially the UK's largest. The buildout at Drax Power Station marks Qatar Investment Authority's Qai's first investment from its $20 billion AI infrastructure venture. Partners plan to invest $3.4 billion over five years, though construction still needs approval and an anchor tenant.
items.title: Qatar and Brookfield Back Supersized UK Data Center

items.summary: Professor Steve Tsang of SOAS's China Institute told FRANCE 24 that, while a weakened Trump could strengthen Beijing's negotiating position, the Chinese leadership views Congress as having limited sway over foreign policy and wants to preserve warm personal ties between the two presidents. The item reports that Democrats took control of both chambers.
items.title: China keeps a close eye on US midterm shake-up

items.summary: As the first week of the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games closed, China topped the medal count with nine golds, three silvers and two bronzes. Japan followed in second place on eight golds, while Egypt placed fourth. South Africa had one gold so far, Kenya won its first women's rugby sevens title, Madagascar earned a historic medal, and host Senegal still awaited its second medal.
items.title: China Leads Medal Count at Dakar Youth Olympics After Week One

items.summary: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double the 65,000 expected by economists, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%. Markets then priced an 85% probability of a quarter-point Fed increase at its December 8-9 meeting, up from around 75%, and moved expectations forward to April. Analysts say the data strengthens the case for tightening as inflation stays above target.
items.title: Strong US jobs report lifts Fed rate-hike bets

items.summary: Pat Gelsinger, former Intel CEO and now with Playground Global, told industry leaders at the International Trade Partners Conference that semiconductor companies have grown complacent. According to a Semafor review of his presentation, he said they are not paranoid enough about new technologies needed for AI performance gains.
items.title: Former Intel CEO Warns Chipmakers of Complacency

items.summary: A healthcare information sharing and analysis center, Health ISAC, issued a security bulletin warning the industry about a wave of cyberattacks on refrigeration controllers that included an incident affecting a major French blood bank. The alert emphasizes operational technology attacks intersect with health-sector threats to patient safety. On Thursday, U.S. cybersecurity agencies published a fact sheet identifying industrial refrigeration and cold-chain systems as critical targets. Investigators consider Iran or Russian-aligned groups responsible, though claims remain unverified due to lack of access logs. Experts warn patching is difficult because downtime risks lifesaving supplies like blood and vaccines.
items.title: Health intel-sharing group warns industry after French blood bank cyberattack

items.summary: Protesters from Geef Tegengas stormed a construction site for a new Microsoft datacentre in Westpoort, Amsterdam, climbing a crane and lighting flares while clashing with police. The action was part of wider European resistance to AI-driven datacentre expansion, separate from the Stop Dirty Data Centres campaign whose members stayed outside the fence. Police said force was used and an officer slightly injured; activists claimed teargas.
items.title: Activists Storm Amsterdam Microsoft Datacentre Site

items.summary: On Friday, Nov 6, Google acquired a data center site in southeast Wyoming from AI infrastructure firm Crusoe, the developer said. The purchase followed Alphabet's $17-billion investment announced Thursday for its first Wyoming facility amid growing political opposition to such projects.
items.title: Google Acquires Crusoe Wyoming Data Center Site

items.summary: Bloomberg News reported on Friday that Microsoft is winding down an arrangement to rent AI computing from Oracle as part of a broader reassessment of billions of dollars in cloud partnerships, citing people familiar with the matter. The report says Microsoft has been turning off rented capacity after declining to renew the contract, and notes Oracle shares fell nearly 3% while Microsoft was little changed.
items.title: Microsoft Wind Down Oracle AI Computing Deal Amid Cloud Review

items.summary: Nashik police named AIMIM leader Imtiyaz Jaleel an accused in a supplementary chargesheet filed Friday for allegedly helping key accused Nida Khan while she was absconding. A lawyer representing one of the victims said the notice under section 35 (3) of the BNSS had been served around a month ago, and that Jaleel did not appear; further proceedings will follow legal procedure. The SIT is probing nine cases dating to July 2022 at TCS's Nashik unit, which maintains a zero-tolerance policy on workplace harassment.
items.title: TCS Nashik Police Name AIMIM Leader in Supplementary Chargesheet

items.summary: OpenAI's CFO Sarah Friar told CNBC that OpenAI will continue its US data-center expansion despite a Democratic midterm sweep raising scrutiny fears. The company dropped non-disclosure agreements with officials and shared construction plans publicly. While the market fell about $2.5 trillion on Thursday, tech firms like Google and ByteDance also pursue new facilities. Friar cited 70 per cent quarterly business growth as demand stays strong.
items.title: OpenAI Advances Data-Center Expansion Amid Political Backlash

items.summary: The Electrek Podcast previews its weekly episode on sustainable transport, highlighting discussion of Tesla ending the Cybertruck, rising electric vehicle sales in several key markets, and additional topics. The live show airs every Friday at 4 p.m. ET on Electrek's YouTube channel, with an accompanying post published afterward.
items.title: Electrek Podcast Covers Tesla Cybertruck Cancellation and EV Market Surge

items.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber, an AI model it says improves on earlier models at finding and validating software vulnerabilities. During testing the model found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox flaws and built exploits for 948 Linux kernel bugs that could grant root access. OpenAI classified it as having Critical cybersecurity capabilities under its Preparedness Framework, up from High for its previous model.
items.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-6 Cyber vulnerability-finding model

items.summary: Delhi Police registered an FIR over alleged circulation of child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms, following directions from the National Human Rights Commission. The Special Cell filed it under Sections 67 and 67B of the Information Technology Act, 2000, after about 10 links were flagged in a complaint. NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo confirmed the action.
items.title: Delhi Police Register FIR Over Alleged CSAM Circulation on Meta Platforms

items.summary: An MIT-developed method called CheMeleon shows that machine learning can outperform existing approaches when data on a target property is scarce. The team, including graduate student Akshat Shirish Zalte and Jackson Burns PhD '26, reported findings in the Sept. 14 issue of the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling. Pre-trained on molecular descriptors from a million PubChem molecules without consulting literature, CheMeleon was used by nine of the top 20 entries in an OpenADMET contest. Zalte noted inquiries began before peer review completed. The model reportedly came out on top across 58 test cases compared with other foundation and classical models.
items.title: MIT Team Unveils Data-Efficient Molecule Prediction Model

items.summary: Elon Musk funded at least $474 million for the 2026 midterms, but Democrats are projected to win 259 House seats and at least 54 Senate seats. The article argues that Congress can use its oversight powers—public hearings, subpoenas—to investigate DOGE’s job cuts and spending. Senator Richard Blumenthal said there is a web of potential corruption worth exploring.
items.title: Democrats Plan Oversight of Musk After DOGE Fallout

items.summary: On Tuesday, Google announced changes that disable Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Google Search for K-12 accounts until administrators re-enable them; Chris Phillips said banned schools would see a message indicating search is unavailable. Critics including Sen. Bernie Sanders called it extortion, while New York City reached out to discuss the update further.
items.title: Google Threatens School Search Access Over AI Bans

items.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer arrested on Oct. 9 for concealing recording devices in an executive conference room, pleaded not guilty Friday at the federal courthouse in San Francisco according to Bloomberg and CNBC. His lawyer filed the plea before Magistrate Judge Peter H. Kang, and he was returned to custody afterward with his attorney declining comment per CNBC. The indictment charges intercepting oral communications; conviction could mean up to five years imprisonment plus a $250,000 fine followed by three years supervised release as stated by the department.
items.title: Former OpenAI Engineer Pleads Not Guilty in Bugging Case

items.summary: This post introduces the Reshard collective, a new NCCL-based communication pattern designed to accelerate reinforcement learning weight refit. During RL post-training, model weights must periodically move from training GPUs to inference GPUs using different parallel layouts, creating large redundant payloads that grow with model size. The authors reformulate refit as resharding a distributed tensor between source and destination layouts, enabling each GPU to receive only its needed shard instead of full parameters. An open-source reference implementation is provided in the NVIDIA NeMo RL framework.
items.title: NVIDIA Introduces Reshard Collective for RL Weight Refit

items.summary: Zyphra has released ZYFA, an open-source Apache 2.0 library of prefill attention kernels in FP8 and BF16 targeting AMD Instinct MI355X (CDNA4) GPUs running ROCm 7.2.3 with PyTorch 2.12. On real model activations at sustained clocks, its FP8 kernels run 1.16-1.76x faster than AITER's default library, while BF16 roughly ties AITER (1.01-1.02x). Real-model gains fall short of Gaussian benchmarks because the MI355X clock depends on operand-bit flips; ZYFA runs at 1,628 MHz versus AITER's 2,108 MHz on Mistral-7B activations while still needing fewer cycles overall. FP8 error sits within a few percent of Composable Kernel and Triton, with KL divergence from fp64 lower than AITER's across full models. Zyphra notes cross-vendor comparisons are limited by differing inputs and clocks and that NVIDIA GPUs were not measured; it recommends benchmarking on real activations at sustained clocks.
items.title: Zyphra Releases ZYFA FP8 FlashAttention for AMD MI355X GPUs

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to increase Cybercab output. The move follows weaker-than-expected sales, recalls and price changes; US 2025 sales reached 20,237 units, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, far below Musk's 2023 target of 250,000. Tesla has issued 11 Cybertruck recalls since late-2023 deliveries began.
items.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production for Cybercab at Texas Factory

items.summary: Nisha Bhagat, an Adivasi leader and social activist aged around 38 in Ranchi, died by hanging at her residence after alleging harassment during a roughly 10-minute livestream. She had called the Pithoria police inspector while live before being rushed to hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival; her body went to RIMS for post-mortem. Police said no suicide note was recovered and an investigation is underway.
items.title: Adivasi Leader Found Dead After Alleging Harassment on Facebook Live

items.summary: Anthropic reported nearly $17 billion in third-quarter revenue, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier, per an amended IPO filing disclosed this month as the company prepares for a potential listing. 'Big Short' investor Michael Burry raised concerns about the figures, writing that the company is priced for optimism and betting its existence on it. He pointed to falling sales-marketing expenses and channel-partner revenue dropping from 48% in early 2026 to nearly 40%. Anthropic said the decline stemmed from lower partner-sourced revenue and changes in distribution terms. Separately, AI-linked stocks fell after Democrats won control of Congress.
items.title: Michael Burry questions Anthropic IPO figures amid AI stock selloff

items.summary: Swedish furniture retailer IKEA reported a third consecutive year of falling sales on Nov 6, citing war-driven cost increases and weak demand from budget-conscious consumers. Group sales reached €43.8 billion (S$63 billion) for the fiscal year ending Aug 31, down 2% versus 2025. CEO Jakub Jankowski said growth must return to make products affordable. Net profit fell to €1.4 billion from €1.5 billion in 2025.
items.title: IKEA CEO Vows Growth After Third Year of Sales Decline

items.summary: Binance suffered the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, with hackers draining roughly US$2.5 billion in a single transaction before ultimately taking about US$3.6 billion overall. According to security firm Blockaid, the thieves exploited EIP-7702, an Ethereum upgrade implemented in May 2025 that lets wallets grant software permission to move funds without separate authorizations for each transfer. The attackers paid around US$15 in network fees to set up this delegation and then moved large sums in one transaction, reducing their exposure. Binance confirmed the attack was sophisticated and said EIP-7702 played a significant role; it has revoked affected permissions and strengthened controls. The FBI attributes the theft to North Korea, which denies involvement.
items.title: Hackers Drain US$2.5b from Binance Using Ethereum Upgrade Shortcut

items.summary: Farooq Abdullah called rebel MLAs’ demands genuine, while Omar Abdullah repeatedly offered to resign amid the National Conference’s worst internal challenge in decades. The rebels sought to replace eight ministers and remove adviser Nasir Aslam Wani; those demands stayed unresolved. Leaders agreed consultative committees per minister and a manifesto committee for election promises, including J&K’s special status. Farooq dismissed split talk, calling the party “united and strong,” while an MLA said all strengthening demands were accepted.
items.title: NC Leaders Defuse Rebel MLA Crisis With Talks and Resignation Offer

items.summary: The Department of Posts announced that India’s only floating post office, housed on a houseboat at Nehru Park on Dal Lake in Srinagar, will now stay open from 9am to 9pm. The extension raises its hours from five to 12 and follows increased footfall and public demand for services beyond regular times, according to chief postmaster general Col Sagar Hanuman Singh.
items.title: India’s Only Floating Post Office Extends Its Hours

items.summary: FIIs increased their buying of Indian equities, investing a net Rs 34,584 crore over the past five trading sessions. On Thursday alone they poured in Rs 14,975 crore, marking the biggest single-day FII purchase in more than a year. This follows months of selling as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to sell.
items.title: Foreign Investors Boost Indian Equity Buying on Friday Amid Market Rally

items.summary: At a November 6 ribbon cutting, Illinois leaders unveiled an IBM Quantum System Two with an Nighthawk r2 processor at the University of Chicago's Hyde Park Labs. Harley T. Johnson, CEO of the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP), called it possibly the most publicly visible quantum computer in the world. The machine supports the National Quantum Algorithm Center, created by the state under a $500 million investment. Officials highlighted decades of regional research talent and recent demonstrations, including one using 70 logical qubits that ran in about 15 minutes.
items.title: Illinois Unveils Quantum Computer in Chicago as Part of National Center Effort

items.summary: The author of a CleanTechnica post reports that Tesla and SpaceX lost $420 billion in market cap following the recent midterm election, which he frames as ironic punishment for Elon Musk's shift toward Republican politics. The piece argues Democrats historically supported clean technology policies benefiting Tesla while Republicans have not, then attributes Musk's political change to specific events including COVID-19 lockdowns, his wealth and tax concerns, his child transitioning, and being excluded from a Biden EV event. It notes Musk donated at least $447 million as the country's largest individual donor in this election, which it says failed about 99.99% of its goal. The author speculates Democrats may investigate or punish Musk for attacks against them but offers no verification that market values have changed since reporting. Figures are reported as stated by CleanTechnica without independent confirmation.
items.title: Tesla and SpaceX Market Cap Falls After Midterm Election

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that Stephen Miller, described as his most controversial aide and architect of the immigration crackdown, would become White House chief of staff days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections. The appointment replaces Susie Wiles, 69, who reportedly resigned Thursday night and was praised by Trump for an outstanding job. Trump said he wanted to make a change and called Miller one of his most trusted advisors. Critics responded sharply, with Democratic congresswoman Becca Balint calling it sickening that Trump promoted the architect of some of the administration’s worst decisions after voters rejected its policies.
items.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff

items.summary: After heavy storms, the Chicago River received billions of gallons of raw sewage. The Racine Avenue pumping station dumped more than 10 billion gallons this year alone—more than any time since 2019—and its North Branch counterpart added nearly 2 billion gallons to the north branch. Officials say intense rains force untreated wastewater into rivers to prevent flooding, despite decades and billions of dollars spent on the Deep Tunnel project. Experts warn the system cannot keep pace with intensifying storms, threatening wildlife and public health.
items.title: Chicago River Overflows With Raw Sewage After Storms

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV has begun his longest overseas trip yet, a 12-day journey across three countries that marks his first major visit since lung cancer surgery to remove part of his right lung. Vatican officials say he finished his two-week recovery and needs no further treatment. The tour starts in Uruguay — famously Latin America's most secular nation, where around 3.5 million people live and only about a third identify as Catholics — before moving to Argentina and ending with a homecoming to Peru, where the pope spent two decades as a missionary priest and bishop of Chiclayo until becoming a naturalized Peruvian in 2015.
items.title: Pope Leo Opens South American Tour in Uruguay After Lung Surgery

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that Stephen Miller, his longtime hardline immigration advisor and domestic policy ideologue, would become chief of staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026. The appointment replaces Susie Wiles, who resigned Thursday night after controversy over her daughter Katie’s $35,000-a-month contract with a lobbying firm tied to the Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Trump made the announcement on his platform Truth, thanking Wiles for her service. At 40, Miller is described as one of the administration’s most despised figures by Democrats, whose hardline views may strain relations with the newly Democratic-controlled Congress.
items.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff

items.summary: The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights asked a court to hold Guatemala responsible for the violent eviction of 14 Maya Q’eqchi’ communities in Alta Verapaz, which cleared land for sugarcane plantations and destroyed traditional crops. The IACHR’s referral said evictions used disproportionate force and left residents without food or safe return. Disputes over unland-titled territory date to at least 2005; a court authorized the removals in 2011 after protests, prompting officials’ claims of threats to governability.
items.title: Guatemala Held Before Human Rights Court Over Indigenous Evictions

items.summary: The Guardian editorial argues that this week’s midterms showed the political cost of the AI boom is arriving, citing a Wall Street wipeout of $3.2tn and crashes at Anthropic, Nvidia and for Elon Musk. It notes influential figures see reality-checking value in the sell-off while Democrats campaigned against datacentre costs to residents. The piece concludes that letting markets decide alone will deepen economic insecurity and political distrust.
items.title: Guardian editorial frames AI sell-off as democratic reckoning

items.summary: Democratic Party figures say they will investigate corruption accusations against the Trump administration, with a focus on its ties to wealthy Middle Eastern countries. President Trump's businesses reportedly earned about $2 billion in income during 2025, roughly triple the previous year, partly from cryptocurrency firm World Liberty Financial, which was sold largely to an investment firm backed by UAE official Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Critics allege connections that the administration denies. Kushner and other deals face scrutiny over conflicts of interest. Ethics watchdogs argue some arrangements create improper influence. Senator Elizabeth Warren said her party would examine related matters including a presidential library project, while investigative journalist Matthew Cole's book alleges Kushner accessed roughly $2 billion in bank accounts through Middle East work he denied.
items.title: Democrats Prioritize Middle East Corruption in Trump Probe

items.summary: CMG reported that China launched remote sensing satellites 07-09 of the Yaogan-51 group from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center in Sichuan Province on November 5, 2026. The three satellites rode a Long March-2C carrier rocket into their preset orbits successfully and are used for scientific experiments and electromagnetic environment detection. The launch marked the 675th mission of the Long March rockets.
items.title: China Launches Yaogan-51 Remote Sensing Satellites

items.summary: A Nigerian Federal High Court voided the nomination of African Democratic Congress presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar and dissolved the party's leadership. The court ruled that interim chairman Nafiu Bala Gombe, rather than David Mark, should have led the party after its former chairman resigned in 2025. ADC officials called the ruling a calculated attempt to weaken their candidacy ahead of elections scheduled for 16 January. Abubakar said he would still contest and listed himself on the electoral commission's candidate list with Rotimi Amaechi as running mate, while Peter Obi expressed concern over uncertainty three months before voting.
items.title: Nigerian Court Voids ADC Presidential Nomination Ahead of January Poll

items.summary: Spain's Maritime Rescue Service rescued about 700 of the roughly 854 migrants it assisted aboard seven small fishing vessels off El Hierro since early Friday morning. Around 350 were transferred to Tenerife on a scheduled ferry, with another 350 planned for an afternoon crossing to ease pressure on reception facilities. Several people required hospital treatment; their exact countries of origin have not yet been established.
items.title: Spain Rescues Nearly 1,000 Migrants Off El Hierro

items.summary: An ABC News article reports that South Australia's political divide over a proposed hyper-scale data centre in Tungkillo, near Mannum, has united the Greens and One Nation at a community rally. The project by Melbourne developer Quantum DC faces strong local resistance over environmental, energy and water concerns. Mid Murray Council Mayor Simone Bailey said it was hard to understand the proposal's benefits, while independent MP Rebekha Sharkie posted that data centres do not belong on prime agricultural land. Premier Peter Malinauskas says law reform is needed before facilities can proceed unless they meet state standards.
items.title: SA Labor warned as data centre opposition unites Greens and One Nation

items.summary: A City of Casey Council survey found that community and family connection was the top factor making residents feel safer, outranking police patrols and CCTV. Besima Goga, a jeweller in Berwick's south-east Melbourne electorate, described break-ins leaving her boss injured and said she now shops with fear. Monash University political scientist Zareh Ghazarian noted voters also weigh infrastructure, crime handling, cost of living and housing affordability. The seat is held by Labor on a 4.7 per cent margin but could lie on a Coalition path to victory. Neighbourhood Houses Victoria CEO Keir Paterson said state funding for local houses had fallen behind costs with capacity at a ten-year low. Early voting begins November 18 before election day on Saturday, November 28.
items.title: Berwick Voters Prioritise Community Safety Over Crime Measures

items.summary: New research from Vals, an AI-capability measurement firm, finds open-weight models now nearly match the best closed ones at complex network hacking. In simulated scenarios on mock corporate networks, OpenAI's trusted-only Daybreak completed 81 percent of tasks while Chinese model DeepSeek finished 73 percent. Runners also cost less—$2 to $3 versus $17 to $46 in tokens for GPT-6-Sol. Vals researcher Nikil Ravi says frontier models are being matched by downloadable open ones, suggesting recent access limits may be moot and urging defenders to prepare within 6, 12 or 24 months. Edera's Alex Zenla called it a possible start of a dangerous landscape, though he noted closed labs likely hold stronger unreleased models.
items.title: Open AI Models Match Closed Ones in Network Hacking Tests

items.summary: FRANCE 24 reports that the Republican Party's midterm defeat has left Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky optimistic about continued support, though he noted Democrats are 'speaking very clearly about supporting Ukraine.' However, analysts caution Congress faces limited scope due to Trump's retained foreign policy authority. James M. Lindsay of the Council on Foreign Relations explained that while the incoming Democratic Congress will be more supportive than the Trump administration, translating preferences into policy remains difficult because the president alone decides negotiation terms.
items.title: Trump's Midterm Loss and Its Implications for US-Ukraine Support

items.summary: Trump administration health officials are expected to miss President Trump's Sunday deadline for new childhood vaccination recommendations, according to people familiar with the matter. Kennedy had promised plans by Nov. 8 but said they would be delivered as ready rather than on schedule. The delay comes amid the largest measles outbreak in decades across 45 states, with 5,182 cases recorded and six deaths confirmed nationally.
items.title: Trump Health Officials Miss Vaccine Recommendation Deadline Amid Measles Outbreak

items.summary: Donald Trump appointed Stephen Miller, age 41 and current deputy chief of staff, as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Trump announced the change on Truth Social, calling Miller one of his most trusted advisors. The appointment comes days after Republicans lost control of both chambers in the midterm elections, amid scrutiny following immigration-enforcement shootings in Minneapolis. Wiles will move to Trump's political operation.
items.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff

items.summary: At the ninth China International Import Expo and Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai on November 5, 2026, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called for joint efforts to achieve balanced trade. He urged greater market openness, deeper investment cooperation, innovation, removal of trade barriers, and making 'the economic pie bigger together' through consultation.
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Calls for Balanced Trade

items.summary: Carolyn Steedman, writing in a letters column, thanked Joe Dunthorne for his investigation of the book club scam. She said she receives two or three such emails monthly and once forwarded one to report@phishing.gov.uk after replying to a sender claiming 500 members would read her books before requesting a fee for distribution. Three other readers replied with their own complaints about recent columns, including Peter Coltman questioning coverage of historical events and Huw Morgan worrying an author might catch cold in the rain.
items.title: Reader thanks journalist for exposing book club scam

items.summary: Two large UK milk processors cut farmgate prices, intensifying pressure on dairy farmers already selling below production cost after a volatile year of drought and high fuel and fertiliser costs. Freshways announced a 7p-a-litre reduction to 29.4p from 1 December, almost undoing earlier increases it had introduced in summer; its managing director Bali Nijjar cited stabilising global markets and rising costs. Arla Foods also cut its standard price by 0.45p to 40.41p while holding organic prices at 58.25p. The NFU called the Freshways move “hugely disappointing,” while farmer Ian Harvey said confidence is “at rock bottom.” Analyst Chris Walkland attributed the cuts to a global oversupply dating back to August 2025 and noted farmers struggle to switch processors easily.
items.title: UK Milk Processors Slash Farmgate Prices Amid Sector Pressure

items.summary: NetLab UFRJ, a Brazilian research group, reports that Meta likely interfered in Brazil's 2026 election. The group created the Big Tech Observatory during the campaign to monitor algorithmic recommendation and political advertising against Electoral Supreme Court rules. It found that between July and September, Meta received approximately R$ 2 million (US$ 400,000) for running 1,613 foreign-placed ads favoring or harming candidates — an estimate hedged by uncertainty over exact figures. The group also identified hundreds of restricted-period ads, fake profiles promoting a nonexistent 'digital vote,' the temporary disabling of Lula's campaign page on September 23, and signs that Lula's campaign may have paid between 33% and 43% more than Flávio Bolsonaro's to reach equal audiences. Meta rejected interference accusations on October 16, attributing the page block to an 'incorrect anti-fraud review.' The group noted transparency limits prevent definitive conclusions about pricing mechanisms.
items.title: Brazilian Research Group Accuses Meta of Election Interference

items.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council announced plans to expand winter support, including new community shops in Pendeford, Graiseley and Bilston. About 17,000 people used the network over six months. Council leader Stephen Simkins said residents still face difficult bill choices. More than 135,000 received cost-of-living support while more than £18.5m was distributed. The council also launched a three-year financial wellbeing strategy and expanded its Community Chefs programme into schools.
items.title: Wolverhampton Council Expands Winter Support for Residents

items.summary: Meta indefinitely delayed a planned change requiring business account users to permit extensive AI training on external websites linked from Facebook, following weeks of backlash. A Meta spokesperson told Reuters the changes were paused while engaging stakeholders and that existing terms remain in effect. Critics warned the vague language could let Meta ignore robots.txt preferences, crawl off-Facebook content for AI training, and avoid licensing fees; courts in Brazil and Norway blocked the terms via injunctions, and the UK's Competition and Markets Authority opened an investigation.
items.title: Meta delays AI-training terms update amid global pushback

items.summary: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are set to make their public debut at Zoo Atlanta on Friday, Nov. 6. The zoo plans an exclusive unveiling of the animals from China. Dr. Gina Ferrie, Vice President of Collections and Conservation, will discuss how her team prepared for the event.
items.title: Zoo Atlanta prepares giant pandas for public debut in November
